## v68 — a fetched page with no `<base>` of its own no longer breaks every relative link

> Fix it now. Make new PR

Direct fix for a real bug found live, mid-testing, reported with a
screenshot: clicking `#bodyContent` (MediaWiki's own "Jump to content"
skip-link) on a real, live-navigated page failed with `cannot resolve
link "#bodyContent": no <base href> on this page to resolve it against`.

**Root cause, confirmed by reading the code, not guessed at**:
`AppEvent::NavResult`'s `Ok` handler only ever set `self.base_url =
find_base_url(&dom.document)` — a fetched page's own `<base href>`, if
it declares one. Most real pages don't (a real browser's own "document
base URL" already defaults to the page's own fetched address when
there's no `<base>` element at all — declaring one is the exception, not
the rule). `snag`'s own bundled pages never hit this because `snag`
itself always synthesizes a `<base href>` reflecting the real fetched
URL when the page doesn't declare its own (v9); `wire`-navigated pages
(v66/v67) never got the equivalent — `FetchedPage` didn't even carry the
URL that was fetched, so `NavResult` had nothing to fall back to.
`base_url` landing at `None` doesn't just break the one link that
happened to be clicked — every relative href on that page breaks the
same way, fragment links included, until the next full navigation.

**Fix**: `FetchedPage` gained a third field, `url: Url` (the real
address `start_navigation` resolved and fetched — already computed,
just not threaded through before). A new, small, directly-testable
`resolve_page_base_url(document, fetched_url) -> Url` — `find_base_url`
if the page declares one, else `fetched_url` — replaces the old bare
`find_base_url(...)` call in `NavResult`'s handler. Mirrors `snag`'s own
v9 behavior exactly, just computed in scratchy itself instead of
pre-baked into the bundle.

**2 new permanent tests** (179 total, up from 177): `resolve_page_base_
url` still prefers a page's own real `<base>` tag when present; and the
exact failure shape itself — a page with no `<base>` and a `<a
href="#bodyContent">` — confirmed to both produce the fetched URL as the
fallback base *and* that `resolve_href` against that base actually
succeeds now (`.../wiki/Example#bodyContent`), not just that the
fallback value looks plausible in isolation. `cargo test`: 179/179.
`cargo clippy --all-targets`: unchanged warning count (21, same as
after v67 — `resolve_page_base_url` is a plain 2-argument function, no
new threading-cost warnings).

**Live-verified by reproducing the exact bug, then confirming the fix,
both as real clicks** — not just trusting the unit tests: a real local
HTTP fixture served a page with no `<base>` tag at all, containing both
a `#bodyContent` fragment link and a genuine root-relative link
(`/relative-page`). A real `xdotool` click through a real running
`wire` daemon onto the fragment link, previously guaranteed to fail,
now re-fetches and re-renders the same page with no error at all
(scratchy has no anchor-scroll feature, so a fragment link is simply a
same-page re-navigation — the point being it *resolves*, not that it
scrolls). A second real click on the genuine relative link correctly
navigated to and rendered the distinct target page. Both confirmed via
screenshot.

**Deliverable**: `scratchy/src/lib.rs` (`FetchedPage::url`,
`resolve_page_base_url`, `start_navigation`'s `FetchedPage` construction
site, `NavResult`'s handler simplified to one line, 2 new tests).

## v69 — command bar QoL: `:visit` renamed to `:go`, Tab completion/cycling, `:help`, `:q`/`:quit`, clipboard paste

> I want to make some qol improvements in the command bar before we
> move to other things, because it's annoying to use right now. First
> rename :view to :go, feels better. Second, I want tab completion and
> cycling in command mode. FInally I want a help page demonstrating all
> the features of the browser. It can get updated as we add more. :q
> should close the browser.

> something I forgot. I should also be able to paste text there (for
> example a URL I got from somwhere else). This is not available by
> default.

Five small, independent requests against the existing `:`-command bar
(itself already landed in the codebase by the time this session started,
but with no `PROMPTS.md` entry of its own — a pre-existing gap this
entry doesn't attempt to backfill, only to build on). The user said
`:view`; the command that actually exists is `:visit` — treated as the
same ask (there's no `:view` today, and "feels better" reads as a
rename, not a request for a second command), confirmed working end to
end before/after, not just assumed.

**`:visit` → `:go`:** one `dispatch_command` match arm renamed, plus
its own and `key_insertion_text`'s doc comments (the latter cited the
old name in a historical bug example — updated to match, since it's
living documentation, not a changelog entry).

**Tab completion/cycling:** two new pure, unit-tested functions —
`token_start_before` (the byte offset of the whitespace-delimited token
ending at the cursor) and `command_completions` (the candidate pool for
that token: `COMMAND_NAMES` for the first token, `SET_ARGS` for `set`'s
own second token, nothing for anything else — deliberately no
completion for `:go`'s own URL argument, which has no finite "correct"
answer to offer). A new `App::completion: Option<CommandCompletion>`
field holds the live cycling state; `App::cycle_command_completion`
completes on the first `Tab` and advances (wrapping) on every
*consecutive* one, reset on any other command-line keystroke
(`handle_command_line_key`'s own top-of-function check) and on
re-entering command mode fresh (`perform_action`'s `EnterCommandMode`
arm) so a stale completion from a previous `:` session can't leak into
a new, empty one.

**`:help`:** a new static page, `src/help.html`, embedded via
`include_str!` the same way `default.css` already is (`HELP_PAGE_HTML`,
next to `DEFAULT_CSS`), shown through `App::show_help` (`parse_html` +
`replace_document`, same shape `show_message` already uses for its own
synthetic pages). Plain semantic HTML — headings, two tables, a list,
`<b>`/`<i>`/`<code>`, an `<hr>`, and a small embedded `data:` PNG — with
no `<style>` of its own, styled entirely by `default.css`, so the page
doubles as a live demo of the default stylesheet rather than a text
dump. Lists every Normal-mode key and command-bar command, including
the ones landing in this same change; expected to be kept current by
whoever changes the command bar next, the same turn they change it.

**`:q`/`:quit`:** `dispatch_command` sets a new `App::should_quit: bool`
— it has no `&ActiveEventLoop` of its own to call `exit()` on directly.
`window_event`'s `WindowEvent::KeyboardInput` arm (the one real call
site with an `ActiveEventLoop` in scope) checks the flag right after
`handle_key_event` returns and calls `event_loop.exit()` there.

**Clipboard paste:** `Ctrl`+`v` inside the command bar, via a new
`arboard = "3.4"` dependency (winit has no clipboard API of its own).
Detected the same way `resolve_binding`'s own `Ctrl`+`d`/`u` arms are —
`Key::Character("v")` guarded on `self.modifiers.control_key()`, ahead
of the plain-insertion catch-all. `TextEditBuffer` gained `insert_str`
(one `insert` per char, control characters — a trailing clipboard
newline being the real case — dropped, since this buffer is always
single-line). A fresh `Clipboard` connection is opened per paste rather
than held on `App` permanently: paste is a rare, user-initiated action,
not a hot path, so there's no real cost to the setup, versus a
permanent connection that would need its own reconnect/`Send` lifecycle
for a feature that doesn't need one. A failed connection or an empty/
unreadable clipboard is a silent no-op, same as a real terminal or
browser's own paste.

**7 new permanent tests** (198 total, up from 191): `token_start_before`
and `command_completions` (prefix-only matching, first-token vs. `set`'s
own second-token candidate pools, no candidates for an arbitrary
argument), and `TextEditBuffer::insert_str` (control characters dropped,
inserts at the cursor rather than always at the end). `App`-level wiring
(`cycle_command_completion`/`apply_completion` replace-range logic,
`paste_into_command_line`, `show_help`, `should_quit`'s path to
`event_loop.exit()`) has no unit test of its own, same "thin
orchestration rests on code review + live verification" category
`start_navigation`'s own click wiring and v67's fetch dispatch already
sit in — verified live instead, below. `cargo test`: 198/198. `cargo
clippy --all-targets`: unchanged warning count (20) — one new
`collapsible_if` in `paste_into_command_line` was fixed with a let-chain
rather than left as a 21st.

**Live-verified against a real running `scratchy` window**, not just
argued: Xvfb (`:99`) plus `xdotool`/`import` (neither was in this
container; installed for this session) stood in for a real X server and
a real keyboard/screenshot, since this environment has no GPU display of
its own. `:help` rendered correctly (headings, both tables, the
embedded image decoded — a real checkered square, not a broken-image
box) and scrolled with `Ctrl`+`d` same as any other page. `Tab` on `:h`
completed to `:help`; a bare `:` cycled `go → help → q → quit → set →
go` across six consecutive `Tab` presses, confirming both the
alphabetical order and the wraparound; `:set ` cycled `novim → vim`.
`Ctrl`+`v` after setting the real X `CLIPBOARD` selection (`xclip
-selection clipboard`) to a URL pasted that exact URL into the command
line. `:go https://example.com/` printed the real resolved HTTP request
to stdout (no `--socket` given), exactly `start_navigation`'s own
documented no-socket behavior — proving the rename routes through the
real navigation path, not just a renamed no-op. `:q` closed the window
and exited the process (confirmed by polling the PID; takes up to ~1.5s
to actually exit under Xvfb, not instant, but it does exit).

**Deliverable**: `scratchy/src/lib.rs` (`COMMAND_NAMES`/`SET_ARGS`,
`CommandCompletion`, `token_start_before`, `command_completions`,
`App::completion`/`should_quit` fields, `App::cycle_command_completion`/
`apply_completion`/`paste_into_command_line`/`show_help`,
`TextEditBuffer::insert_str`, `dispatch_command`'s `:go`/`:help`/`:q`/
`:quit` arms, `window_event`'s `should_quit` check, 7 new tests);
`scratchy/src/help.html` (new); `scratchy/Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`
(`arboard` dependency added).

## v70 — `:q` from `:help` goes back, instead of quitting

> :q from the help page should bring the user back to their previous
> page, similar to how vim closes the buffer in those cases

A follow-up on v69's `:help`, filed the same session right after seeing
it work: `:q` previously quit scratchy outright no matter what was on
screen, which made `:help` a dead end — closing it meant closing the
whole browser. Real vim's own `:q` doesn't work that way: it closes the
current buffer/window and falls back to whatever was open before it,
only actually quitting once there's nothing left to fall back to. That's
the exact shape asked for and the exact shape built.

**What/why:** a new `App::pre_help_page: Option<SavedPage>`, where
`SavedPage` snapshots every piece of per-page state `replace_document`
either changes or clears (`document`, `extra_css`, `image_cache`,
`scroll_offset`, `scroll_offsets` — not `base_url`, since `show_help`'s
own `replace_document` call never touches it in the first place).
`show_help` snapshots into it, but only when it's already `None` —
re-running `:help` while already viewing it must not let the help page
itself get captured as "the page to go back to." `dispatch_command`'s
`:q`/`:quit` arm now branches on `pre_help_page`: `Some` pops it
(`App::restore_saved_page`, the mirror image of the snapshot — restores
the three fields `replace_document` always zeroes instead of leaving
them zeroed, scroll position included, since closing `:help` isn't
supposed to look like navigating to a new page); `None` falls back to
the previous behavior (`should_quit`). `start_navigation`'s own first
line unconditionally drops `pre_help_page`: a real navigation (a real
click, or `:go`) while `:help` happens to be open means the page about
to show is genuinely new, not an overlay on top of whatever `:help`
saved — a later `:q` from there should quit, not resurrect a page from
before `:help` was ever opened. `src/help.html`'s own `:q`/`:quit` row
updated to describe both halves.

No new unit tests — same "thin App-level orchestration rests on code
review + live verification" category v69's own `cycle_command_
completion`/`paste_into_command_line` already sit in, not a gap: there's
no new pure, stateless function here to unit-test, just `SavedPage`
plumbing through existing `App` methods. `cargo test`: still 198/198
(unchanged). `cargo clippy --all-targets`: unchanged warning count (20).

**Live-verified against a real running window** (same Xvfb/`xdotool`/
`import` setup v69 used), four scenarios, not just the one asked for:
(1) scrolled a real page down, opened `:help`, scrolled *that* down to a
different position, ran `:q` — landed back on the original page at the
exact same scroll offset (pixel-identical screenshot to before `:help`
was opened), process still running. (2) `:q` with no `:help` open still
quits for real (polled the PID: exits a couple seconds later, same as
v69). (3) Opened `:help`, opened `:help` *again*, then `:q` — landed on
the real original page, not stuck on the help page itself (confirms the
"snapshot only once" guard). (4) Opened `:help`, then ran a real `:go`
to navigate away, then `:q` — this time it quit instead of popping back,
confirming `start_navigation`'s own clear takes effect.

**Deliverable**: `scratchy/src/lib.rs` (`SavedPage`, `App::
pre_help_page`, `App::restore_saved_page`, `show_help`'s snapshot guard,
`dispatch_command`'s `:q`/`:quit` arm, `start_navigation`'s clear);
`scratchy/src/help.html` (`:q`/`:quit` row updated).

## Q1 — `SCRATCHY_CSS_DEBUG` tells failures apart (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q1) of the ranked QUEUE in
> scratchy/TODO.txt.

**What changed:** `DeclParser::parse_value`'s per-property dispatch moved
into `DeclParser::apply`. When a declaration leaves `Declarations`
unchanged, it is re-applied to a blank `Declarations`. It is reported as
`ignored` only if that also sets nothing, so duplicate-valued
declarations stay silent. Selectors that fail to parse are reported as
`dropped selector `<text>``, and dropped at-rules as `dropped @<name>`
(from the `StyleSheetParser` errors in `parse_stylesheet` and the nested
`@media` loop). All lines go through `css_debug_report`, which a test can
capture via a thread-local. Test:
`css_debug_distinguishes_duplicates_dropped_selectors_and_at_rules`.
No grim screenshot: output-only diagnostic on stderr.

---

## Q2 — dropped pseudo-classes now parse (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q2) of the ranked QUEUE in
> scratchy/TODO.txt.

**What changed:** `OurPseudoClass` gained `NeverMatches(name)` (for
`:hover`, `:active`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible`, `:focus-within`,
`:target`), `Checked`, `Disabled`, `Enabled`, `Dir(ltr)` and `Lang(x)`.
`OurSelectorParser` parses the plain ones and, through a new
`parse_non_ts_functional_pseudo_class`, `:dir()` and `:lang()`.
`match_non_ts_pseudo_class` implements them per the queue spec (`:lang`
walks ancestors via `parent_handle`; new free fn `is_form_control`).
Tests: `q2_state_pseudo_classes_parse_and_match`,
`q2_checked_disabled_enabled_match_elements`. No grim screenshot:
`grim` fails in this sandbox ("failed to copy output eDP-1"), so the
Wikipedia "Jump to content" check is unverified by a real render.

## Q3 — pseudo-elements parse and are skipped (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q3) of the ranked QUEUE in
> scratchy/TODO.txt.

**What changed:** `NoPseudoElement` is replaced by `OurPseudoElement`
(`Named(&'static str)` for `before`, `after`, `marker`, `placeholder`,
`selection`, `first-line`, `first-letter`, `backdrop`,
`file-selector-button`; `Vendor(String)` for `-webkit-*`/`-moz-*`/`-ms-*`).
`OurSelectorParser::parse_pseudo_element` parses them, so
`a, a::after{..}` keeps its `a` part. `match_pseudo_element` returns
false, so a selector carrying one never matches an ordinary element.
`matching_declarations` ignores pseudo-element selectors when computing a
rule's specificity. The Q1 debug test now uses `p::bogus` as its dropped
selector. Test: `q3_pseudo_elements_parse_but_never_match_elements`.
`grim` worked this time; a simple page rendered normally (link and
paragraph, nothing generated from pseudo-elements).

---

## Q4 — per-side borders (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q4) of the ranked QUEUE in
> scratchy/TODO.txt.

**What changed:** `Declarations` and `ComputedStyle` now hold
`border_width`/`border_color`/`border_style` as `[_; 4]` arrays in
top/right/bottom/left order (`SIDE_NAMES`). New `parse_border_property`
(called from the declaration parser) handles `border`, the box-syntax
`border-width/-color/-style` (1 to 4 values, via `parse_box4`), the 4 side
shorthands and the 12 side longhands. `resolve_style` zeroes a side's width
when its style is `none`/`hidden`. Layout reads `ComputedStyle::border_top/
border_left/border_h/border_v` instead of `2.0 * border_width`.
`paint_box_decoration` keeps the old `paint_border`/`fill_rounded_ring`
path when all four sides are identical, and otherwise paints each side
with its own width/style/color (bevel styles degrade to solid;
`border-radius` falls back to square corners). Test:
`q4_per_side_borders_parse_and_resolve`. `grim` worked: a div with
`border-bottom: 4px solid red; border-left: 6px dashed blue` showed only
those two sides.

---

## Q4b — per-side border joins, radius and bevels (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q4b) of the ranked QUEUE in
> scratchy/TODO.txt.

**What changed:** the non-uniform branch of `paint_box_decoration` now calls
the new `paint_per_side_border`, a per-pixel painter: each border-band
pixel goes to the side it is proportionally closest to (distance / width),
giving diagonal mitered corners; the outer edge is rounded by
`border-radius` and the inner edge by `radius - width` per axis
(`in_rounded_rect`); `border_pixel_color` evaluates solid/dashed/dotted/
double and the four bevel styles per side. `round` is now true for any
non-uniform border (the background rounds too). Test:
`q4b_per_side_borders_miter_round_and_bevel`. `grim` worked: a div with red
top, dashed blue left and double green bottom borders and `border-radius:
24px` showed rounded, mitered corners. Left out: dashed/dotted/double/bevel
uniform borders still go square with `border-radius` (see QUEUE Q4c).

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q5) of the ranked QUEUE in

## Q7 — CSS-wide keywords (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q7) of the ranked QUEUE in
> scratchy/TODO.txt.

**What changed:** `DeclParser::apply` recognizes `inherit`/`initial`/`unset`/`revert`/`revert-layer` (optionally followed by `!important`) for color, background/background-color, display, font-size, line-height, vertical-align, font-family, font-weight, text-align, white-space, cursor and visibility, storing them in `Declarations::wide` (mutually exclusive with the typed field; last declaration in a rule wins). `cascade_css` lets a keyword compete at its own specificity/source order/important tier, and `apply_wide` resolves it (`revert` = `unset`; `unset` = inherit for inherited properties, initial otherwise). `InheritedStyle` gained the parent's `background_color`, `display` and `vertical_align` so `inherit` works on those non-inherited properties. Test: `q7_css_wide_keywords_inherit_initial_unset_revert`. `grim` worked: `<p style="color:inherit">` under a red div rendered red. Left out: keywords on other properties (margin, border, etc.) are still ignored; `background: inherit` only covers the colour, not the image.

## Q13 — Custom properties that cascade per element (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q13) of the ranked QUEUE in
> scratchy/TODO.txt.

**What changed:** the whole-stylesheet textual `var()` pass (`collect_root_custom_props`) is gone. A declaration whose value contains `var(` is now stored raw in `Declarations::var_decls` at parse time. `resolve_style` computes the element's custom properties with `compute_custom_props` (parent's table plus its own `--x` declarations by specificity/order, inline last; values substituted against the combined table, a cycle invalidates the whole cycle so `var()` takes its fallback), then re-parses each matched rule's `var_decls` (and the inline style) with the table substituted (`expand_var_decls`/`merge_var_matches`) and slots the results into the normal cascade. The table travels as `custom_props: Option<&'static CustomProps>` on `InheritedStyle`/`ComputedStyle` (interned and leaked per distinct table so both stay `Copy`). `substitute_css_vars` now takes a lookup closure and skips quoted strings. `resolve_background_image` takes the element's table too. `var()` inside `calc()` now works. Tests: `custom_prop_on_ancestor_inherits_to_subtree`, `custom_prop_not_visible_outside_its_subtree`, `descendant_overrides_custom_prop`, `chained_custom_props_resolve`, `custom_prop_cycle_uses_fallback`, `var_inside_quoted_string_is_not_substituted`, `var_inside_calc_resolves_per_element`, `background_image_var_resolves`, `inline_style_custom_prop_and_var` (the old `non_root_custom_prop_is_not_picked_up` test was replaced, its premise is gone). `grim` worked: `:root{--a;--b:var(--a)}` chained into a red paragraph, and `.dark{--bg;--w:calc(...)}` applied to a descendant `p` two levels down (blue background, 300px wide). Left out: within one rule a `var()` declaration is ordered after that rule's plain ones regardless of source order; CSS comments inside values are not skipped by the substituter.

## Q23c — Flex leftovers: column min size, column wrap, baseline, §9.7 loop (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q23c, flex leftovers) of the ranked QUEUE in scratchy/TODO.txt, all of it in one PR.

**What changed:** (1) `resolve_flex_main_sizes` is now the real CSS Flexbox §9.7 freeze-and-retry loop (initial freezing by factor 0 or hypothetical-vs-basis, the `sum of factors < 1` rule, min/max violation freezing), so a clamped item's under/overshoot is redistributed among its unclamped siblings. (2) `measure_flex_column` gets the automatic minimum size: with `height:auto`, `overflow:visible` and no `min-height`, an item's floor is its measured content height (clamped to its basis); an explicit `height` keeps a floor of 0 (the content height would need a second measure). (3) `measure_flex_column` implements `flex-wrap` / `wrap-reverse` for a container with a definite height: greedy column breaking, per-column cross size from the widest margin box, `align-content` over the free width, and the new shared `distribute_align_content` (the row code now uses it too). Wrapped items are measured once at fit-content width and stretched by overwriting `Laid::w` (no re-measure, so no duplicate positioned-descendant entries); this also now applies the items' horizontal margins in column containers. (4) `align-items: baseline` in rows: new `first_baseline` finds the first shaped line's baseline through the shape cache (fallback: border-box bottom), items shift to share the line's baseline and the line cross size covers the above/below extents. Tests: `q23c_flexible_lengths_freeze_clamped_items_and_redistribute`, `q23c_column_items_do_not_shrink_below_their_content_height`, `q23c_column_wrap_makes_side_by_side_columns`, `q23c_baseline_alignment_lines_up_first_text_baselines`. `grim` worked: three 60px boxes in a 130px column wrap became red/green over blue-to-the-right, and a 40px "Big" and 12px "small" shared a baseline. Left out (nothing re-queued): column wrap without a definite height (stays one column), baseline for items whose first line is in a mixed-inline run or an image (falls back to the bottom edge), `wrap-reverse` flipping flex-start/flex-end meaning for rows, `last baseline`, and re-measuring stretched wrapped items at the final column width.

## Q25 — `box-shadow`: blur, multiple shadows, inset, currentColor (queue item)

> Implement the first unchecked item (Q25, `box-shadow`) of the ranked QUEUE in scratchy/TODO.txt.

**What changed:** `BoxShadow` gained `blur`, `inset` and an optional color (missing or `currentColor` resolves to the element's own `color`); `parse_box_shadow` now parses a comma-separated list (`parse_box_shadow_layer` per layer) into a fixed `[Option<BoxShadow>; MAX_SHADOWS]` (4; extras ignored, because `ComputedStyle` is `Copy`). `ComputedStyle::box_shadow` is now that array of `ResolvedBoxShadow`. New `paint_box_shadow` rasterizes the shadow shape (rounded by `border-radius` plus/minus spread) into an f32 coverage mask, blurs it with `blur_mask` (3-pass box blur, sigma = blur/2, margin 1.5*blur), and composites per pixel: outer shadows skip the border box itself (so a transparent box shows no shadow through it), inset ones are confined to the padding box and use the inverse coverage. Outer layers paint before the background, inset after the border/outline, first-listed on top. Masks over 4M cells fall back to a hard edge. Tests: `q25_box_shadow_parses_multiple_inset_blur_and_current_color`, `q25_blurred_outer_shadow_fades_and_skips_the_border_box`, `q25_inset_shadow_paints_inside_and_multiple_layers_stack`; the two older `box-shadow` tests were adjusted to index `[0]`. `grim` worked: a rounded box with a soft drop shadow, a blue inset glow and a hard red offset shadow. Left out (nothing re-queued): inset shadows are not clipped by an inner rounded border's elliptical shape beyond the uniform radius, shadows are not anti-aliased at the shape edge, shadows beyond 4 layers are dropped, and the blurred shadow of a box wider than ~2000px loses its blur.

> Implement Q31b of the ranked QUEUE in scratchy/TODO.txt: `:target` (needs fragment navigation), scroll-into-view on Tab focus, and a default focus ring. Form controls stay with Q30.

**What changed:** `OurPseudoClass::Target` replaces the never-matching placeholder and reads the new `InteractionState::target` (`STATE_TARGET` in the restyle mask). `fetch_url` now treats a link that differs from the current page only by fragment as same-document: `apply_fragment` sets `:target` and scrolls the element to the top; cross-page links with a fragment carry it in `pending_fragment` until the new layout has the element (`ShapeResult`). **What changed:** Q34a: `Floats` now holds its two lists in `RefCell`s and the `Blocks` arm of `measure` pushes into the set it was handed instead of a clone, so a float lives for its whole BFC (a later `<section>` wraps around it and `clear` sees it). Fresh sets still start at every BFC boundary. Q34b: new `ComputedStyle::establishes_bfc` (float, `overflow` != visible, `display: flow-root` via the new `flow_root` flag, block-level table/flex/grid). A BFC root in flow is placed in the corridor `avail_bounds` leaves (dropping below the next float if its min-content width doesn't fit, `Floats::next_bottom`), gets a fresh `Floats` for its own content, and its auto height grows to contain its floats. Q34c: new `table_caption`/`caption_bottom` style flags (`display: table-caption`, `caption-side`); `cell_natural_width` gives a `display: table` box only the caption's min-content width, `measure_table` lays `caption-side: bottom` captions after the grid, and a floated/absolute `display: table` now stays a table (CSS2.1 §9.7) with `measure_table` taking the shrink-to-fit override. Tests: `float_in_one_section_affects_text_and_clear_in_the_next_section`, `bfc_root_beside_a_float_is_narrowed_to_the_corridor`, `flow_root_contains_its_own_floats`, `table_caption_does_not_widen_a_shrink_to_fit_table_and_wraps_below`. `grim` of the Nvidia page at ~1057px: the History border now ends at the infobox's left edge. Left out: Q34d (blank runs mid-line in the lead paragraph) still reproduces; headless layout places every word, so it is a paint/live-width issue, details in TODO.txt. `caption-side` is not inherited; `cell_natural_width` ignores an explicit `width` on a non-image block (so a `width:110px` empty div contributes 0 to a shrink-to-fit table).

## Q34d — blank words mid-line in progressive layout (queue item)

> work on Q34d

**What changed:** the missing words were not a paint bug. A headless layout of the saved Nvidia page placed every word and painted them all, but a headless *progressive* run (tiny deadline, same `ShapeCache`, `next_id` reset, like the shaping worker) reproduced empty `w=0` words. `measure_mixed_inline` took a fresh `next_id` for each word of a chunk that split across wrapped lines, so the ids consumed depended on line breaks, which differ between passes; later ids shifted onto other paragraphs' cache entries. Each chunk word now reserves its fallback id up front (`WordSource::Chunk::word_id`). Test: `mixed_inline_id_consumption_does_not_depend_on_line_breaks` (4 ids at width 5000 vs 248 at 300 before the fix; equal after). `grim` of the live Nvidia page: "Nvidia became the first company to surpass US$4 trillion" is complete. Left out: the whole-buffer vs per-word path choice (`content_y < floats.max_bottom()`) can also change the id count between passes if placeholder heights differ; not observed on a real page yet (noted in TODO.txt). A first synthetic regression test that ran progressive passes did not reproduce the bug, so the test checks the id-count invariant directly.

## Q36 — colspan/rowspan in measure_table (queue item, out of order at user's request)

> implement Q36 (colspan/rowspan in measure_table)

**What changed:** `ComputedStyle` gained `col_span`/`row_span` (set by `build_table_row_cells` from the attributes, clamped to 1000/65534). New `table_grid_placement` assigns each cell a start column, skipping columns held by a `rowspan` cell from an earlier row. `table_column_widths` sizes columns from single-column cells first, then widens the spanned columns only if a spanning cell needs more (shortfall split in proportion to current width). `lay_out_row_cells` takes the placement and gives a cell the summed width of its spanned columns. `settle_rowspans` runs after the rows are laid out: a rowspan cell gets the summed height of its rows, the last spanned row grows if the cell is taller, and later rows shift down. Tests: `colspan_header_spans_both_columns_without_squeezing_them`, `cell_after_colspan_cell_lands_in_the_following_column`, `rowspan_cell_takes_summed_row_height_and_pushes_the_next_column_over`. Left out: `rowspan="0"`, `<col span>` widths, `table-layout: fixed`.

## Q33c3 — transparent text painted opaque (queue item)

> Do ONLY Q33c3: the portal's language select has `color:transparent` but its option text still paints over the EN label.

**What changed:** two real bugs, neither select-specific. (1) `paint_text` used cosmic-text's `LegacyRenderer`, whose callback receives the glyph mask coverage as the colour's alpha and drops the span colour's own alpha, so any `color` with alpha < 1 (incl. `transparent`) painted fully opaque; each glyph's alpha is now stashed in a `Cell` and multiplied back, alpha-0 glyphs are skipped. (2) `to_text_color` only handled `CssColor::Rgba`, so `hsl()/hsla()/hwb()` colours were silently dropped (the portal's `color: hsla(0,0%,100%,0)` fell back to black); Hsl and Hwb now convert. Test `q33c3_*`. 392 tests pass. (3) `style.rs`: an `option` inside `select` takes the select's colour, since the closed select paints in its own colour and the portal sets `select option{color:grey}`. Test `q33c3_option_in_select_*`. Portal grim: only "EN" shows, no "Afrikaans" overlap. WPT: hwb-002 and t425-hsla-values-b newly pass (expectations updated).

## Build-test investigation (Opus, docs only)

> Investigate user reports on https://wikipedia.org (the donation dialog shows and Close does nothing; `TypeError: not a function` at index-be66aee782.js:1:18546; `Io error: Broken pipe` then an `ExitFailure(1)` panic in `run()`), then run a broad live test pass and file every bug found. No source changes.

**What changed:** docs only: REGRESSIONS.md R8–R11, and TODO.txt QB1–QB10 at the top of the QUEUE. Findings:
- The Broken-pipe panic happens when the compositor drops scratchy after a main-thread stall. Reproduced; hover restyles stall the main thread for 0.2–1.8 s.
- JS DOM writes skip the restyle path, so pages that write the DOM on a timer stay blank or lose text.
- `:help` keeps the previous page's JS running.
- The dialog doesn't show on current `main` (Q33c2 hides closed dialogs), but `showModal`/`close` don't exist. Neither does `focus()`, which is the portal's last JS error.

Clicks, keys and scrolling were driven in a nested dwl through the virtual-pointer and virtual-keyboard protocols; the recipe is in REGRESSIONS.md.

## QB5 — focus()/blur(), autofocus, window.scroll* (queue item)

> Implement QB5 from the TODO.txt queue (R11c): `Element.focus()`/`blur()`, `autofocus` reflection, `window.scroll/scrollTo/scrollBy`; clears the wikipedia.org portal's last JS error.

**What changed:** `JsRequests` (in `js_dom.rs`, drained by `JsEngine::take_requests` in `App::js_sync`) carries a pending focus/blur and a pending scroll, the same shape as the QB2 dirty flag. `HTMLElement.prototype.focus/blur` call `__d_focus`, which records a request only for focusable elements (`is_focusable` plus enabled input/button/select/textarea); `js_sync` then calls `set_focus_element` (so focus/blur events fire from the existing Q33d code) and `scroll_focus_into_view`. `blur()` only clears focus when the element is the focused one. `window.scroll/scrollTo/scrollBy` (numbers or `{top,left}`) set `App::scroll_offset` (clamped at 0 here, at the bottom by `redraw`); `scrollX/scrollY` follow optimistically. `autofocus`, `disabled`, `required`, `checked` are boolean attribute reflections. Tests: `qb5_focus_and_blur_are_functions_and_record_requests`, `qb5_autofocus_and_boolean_attributes_reflect`, `qb5_window_scroll_family_records_a_request`, and `qb5_app_applies_requests` (inside the shared event-loop test `qb2_js_dom_writes_use_restyle_path`; skipped without a display).

**What changed:** `hover_idle_wait` (pure, in layout.rs) gates `App::hover_restyle_delay`: when the last `build_layout_tree_with_resources` took over 50 ms, hover waits for 150 ms without `CursorMoved` (`last_pointer_move`, `last_build_time` on `App`). `JsEngine::eval_value` (timers, events) uses `CALLBACK_BUDGET` = 500 ms and logs when it is hit; page-load scripts keep 5 s. ## QY5 Script budget in CPU time, clear interrupt message

> Implement QY5 (R20 error 4): clear log line when a script/callback is stopped by the interrupt budget, and measure the budget in thread CPU time instead of wall-clock; keep the 5 s / 500 ms values.

**What changed:** js.rs `thread_cpu_nanos()` (`libc::clock_gettime(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)`; `libc = "0.2"` added as a direct dependency, already in Cargo.lock transitively). The interrupt deadline is now thread-CPU nanoseconds, armed per top-level eval; the handler sets a `tripped` flag and `eval`/`eval_value` log `js: <name> stopped: exceeded the 5 s CPU-time page-load budget (<N> KB of source)` (or `500 ms ... callback budget`) instead of `InternalError: interrupted`. Compile time of a huge script still counts as CPU (QuickJS has no hook to exclude it); only machine load and waiting no longer do. Tests `qy5_*`.

## Fix flaky q33t_timer_args_string_handler_raf_and_order

> The test fails in ~2 of 3 parallel full cargo test runs but passes alone. Diagnose with evidence and make it deterministic by fixing the test, not the product.

**What changed:** root cause: the test pumped timers against the real wall clock. The 30 ms setTimeout, the 1 ms string timeout and the rAF (due at the next 16.7 ms frame boundary, i.e. anywhere from ~0 to 16.7 ms after registration) are each stamped with `__scratchy_now()` at their own registration, so any stall between statements (CPU contention under parallel builds) or an unlucky frame phase reorders them. Added `start_scripts_clocked` in js.rs (optional manual clock behind `__scratchy_now`; `start_scripts` passes None, so behaviour is unchanged) and a `#[cfg(test)]` `next_due_ms`; the test helper `run_with_timers` now jumps the manual clock to each next due time (no real sleeping). All assertions kept.

## Q35b2 debounce image-triggered relayouts

> Implement Q35b2: each arriving image (`ImageFetched`) sets `layout_dirty` and costs a full relayout. Defer the rebuild while one is in flight and add a short debounce so a burst collapses into one rebuild, without delaying the first layout or leaving an image unflushed; keep the R2/R7/QB2 invariants. Measure first.

**What changed:** app.rs `handle_image_fetched` still caches the image immediately but records `image_relayout_since` and arms an `AppEvent::ImageFlush` timer (`IMAGE_RELAYOUT_DEBOUNCE`, 80 ms from the first arrival, layout.rs, with the pure `image_relayout_wait`). `flush_image_relayout` (timer and the complete `ShapeResult`) sets `layout_dirty`/bumps `layout_generation` only when the window passed and no pass is in flight/holding the old frame, so a burst is one rebuild and never makes an in-flight pass stale. An arrival while `layout_dirty` (first layout) is a no-op; `replace_document` clears the pending state. Measured (temporary `Instant` prints, removed, unloaded machine) on en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page: 28 ImageFetched either way; builds 3 heavy (about 360 ms each) + 5-8 trivial before, 2 heavy after; all complete frames: before final complete frame ~4.95 s, after ~5.1-5.2 s (an intermediate complete frame with most images appears at ~4.4 s). Main-thread build time dropped by about one build (~360 ms). Tests `q35b2_*` (the pure one runs without a display; the handler one returns early without one; both fail without the fix). The paint-only patch pass stays out of scope.

> Implement QY10: `window.matchMedia(query)` returning a MediaQueryList (matches, media, addListener/removeListener, addEventListener, onchange) reusing the CSS media-query code; invalid query gives matches false and media 'not all'; duckduckgo and youtube call it at startup.

**What changed:** css.rs: `media_query_string_matches(query, w, h)` evaluates a query string (comma lists, `not`/`only`, `and`/`or`, nested conditions, level-4 range syntax, width/height/orientation/resolution/hover/pointer/prefers-*/forced-colors/color etc.; unknown features are false, invalid items become `not all`) and reuses `media_feature_length_px` for lengths. The existing `MediaQuery` struct was not extended, so `@media` CSS behaviour is unchanged. js.rs: native `__scratchy_media`, `MediaQueryList` (an EventTarget; `matches`/`media` re-evaluated per read) and `window.matchMedia`. Viewport is the fixed 1024x768 and `change` never fires (QY10a). Tests `qy10_*` (3).

## Page JS network queue (QF7)

> Implement TODO.txt QF7: the engine/App plumbing that lets page JS send a request and receive the answer without exposing `fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest` (QF8/QF9). JS glue `__net_request` in src/fetch_prelude.js (AbortSignal, Response via `__make_response`). Sync mode on the engine thread with `sync_xhr_timeout_ms`. `--js-report` runs the queue and prints a `--- network ---` section, with the `<base href>` as page URL. Fake executor for unit tests.

**What changed:** new src/js_net.rs (`NetJob`, `NetExecutor`/`WireExecutor`/`NoSocketExecutor`, `NetScheduler`, `NetState`, `install_net`, `deliver_net`, `drive_report_net`, `format_net_report`); src/js_dom.rs (`JsRequests.net/net_done/net_abort`); src/js.rs (engine `net` state, log levels `net`/`net-warning`, report loop, base-href page URL); src/app.rs (`AppEvent::JsNet`, `NetScheduler` in `App`, `pump_net`, `handle_js_net`, parked results for `:help`); src/fetch_prelude.js (`__net_request`, `__net_complete`). ## QY34: script-inserted `<script>` elements run (2026-11-17)

> Item QY34 (R26). Scripts made with `createElement('script')` and connected never ran, no request, no event. Implement "prepare the script element": inline runs synchronously (currentScript set), `src` goes through the QF7 queue (api `script`: RequestPolicy, CORS for `crossorigin`, no-cors keeps the body for the engine only) and runs as its own task, then `load`/`error`; `type=module` via the QY15 loader (graph fetched through the queue, registered in the loader's now run-time-growable source map); moved scripts are not re-run; `type`/`nomodule`/`language` checks; `async=false` keeps insertion order.

**What changed:** src/js_dom.rs (QY34 block after the HTMLScriptElement protos: eligibility by createElement/cloneNode, sweep after `afterIns`/`__d_settext`/`src` setattr), src/js.rs (`install_script_natives`: `__scratchy_run_global` with the QY22 budget split, `__scratchy_utf8`, `__mod_*`), src/js_modules.rs (`ModuleStore.sources` is a RefCell), src/js_net.rs (`NetMeta.script`, opaque script answers keep status/body), src/fetch_prelude.js (`raw` request flag), tests `qy34_*` in src/tests.rs. Limits: innerHTML/document.write scripts never run (spec); no MIME/nosniff check; no `integrity`; scripts connected by one insertion run in creation order, not tree order; module evaluation of a fetched module runs under the callback budget; `data:` script URLs are not decoded.

## QY44a: stop draining promise jobs after a budget kill (2026-11-17)

> Item QY44a (R29). A CPU-budget trip in one promise job kept `drain_jobs` running the later jobs on an already-expired deadline, so each was killed part-way (QuickJS's interrupt is uncatchable and skips `finally`), leaving library state stale (kevlar signals: ``sb`kCcqO`` x84 on YouTube).

**What changed:** js.rs `drain_jobs` breaks out after the first job killed by the budget and leaves the rest queued in QuickJS; it logs one line per tripping turn ("1 job killed, remaining jobs deferred to the next turn"), never one per job. `next_deadline` (App loop) and `next_due_ms` (`--run-timers`) report "due now" while jobs are pending, and `run_due_counted` counts a turn that only ran deferred jobs, so they run next turn under a fresh `CALLBACK_BUDGET`. Tests: new `qy44a_tripped_job_does_not_kill_later_jobs` (R29 `trip_jobs_big` fixture inline: `[job2,job3]` and empty stack); `qy22_tripped_job_drain_logs_one_line_with_a_count` now expects one line per tripping turn (not one overall) because deferred jobs now spread across turns. Verified: full suite 780 passed, WPT no change (271/271), clippy 78, wikipedia.org / en.wikipedia / HN 0 errors, github/duckduckgo/guardian/bbc/lobste.rs unchanged before/after. The YouTube ``sb`` flood did not reproduce in any cached copy today (0 before AND after in 3+2 runs each at load 2-6), so only the fixture proves the fix. Limit: the one job that actually exceeds the budget is still killed.

## QY43: preserved newlines break lines in the per-word inline path (2026-11-17)

> Item QY43 (R28). `measure_mixed_inline` split words only on spaces, so a preserved "\n" (pre/pre-wrap/pre-line) in a paragraph with an inline-block or padded inline never became a line break and words overprinted (YouTube history-off card subtitle).

**What changed:** layout.rs: `SpanStyle.white_space` (the white-space of the element the text sits in; YouTube's `yt-formatted-string{white-space:pre-wrap}` is an inline element in a `normal` block, so the paragraph's own value is not enough); the Text arm of `measure_mixed_inline` splits a text item at '\n' when its span preserves newlines and emits `Measured::Break` between the segments (blank lines give empty lines); each segment is its own chunk. css.rs: `WhiteSpace` derives Debug. Tests: qy43_* in tests.rs. Verified on youtube.com in a nested dwl (before: overprint; after: clean lines plus link).

## QJ6: element scrolling (scratchy/qj6-element-scrolling)

**Prompt:** `el.scroll/scrollTo/scrollBy`, `scrollTop/scrollLeft` setters that really scroll overflow:auto/scroll containers, and scrollIntoView through ancestor scroll containers (QJ5 only scrolled the window). vim.js scrolls its help buffer with element scrollTop and needs scrollTop/scrollHeight/clientHeight to agree.

**What changed:** scratchy already had nested scroll regions (v62: `overflow: scroll/auto` Blocks boxes get a `ScrollInfo`, the wheel routes to the deepest one, paint/hit-test shift children by `App::scroll_offsets` keyed by a per-layout id; vertical only; no wheel routing into positioned/fixed boxes). QJ6 adds `ScrollInfo::node` and `App::node_scroll` (offsets keyed by DOM node, re-applied to the new tree after every layout install, so they survive relayouts); js_dom.rs: natives `__d_nid`/`__d_scrollel`, `JsRequests.el_scroll`, `Element.scroll/scrollTo/scrollBy`, scrollTop setter clamped to scrollHeight-clientHeight (auto/scroll boxes only), a `scroll` event queued on change, getBoundingClientRect/getClientRects subtract scrolled ancestors (the walk only happens once something has scrolled), scrollIntoView scrolls each scrollable ancestor then the window; `JsEngine::set_scroll` also pushes wheel-changed element offsets back to script. Tests `qj6_*`. Limits (QJ6b): no scrollLeft/horizontal, overflow:hidden not programmatically scrollable, no wheel into fixed/absolute scroll boxes, no scroll event for wheel scrolls, no smooth behaviour.

**What changed:** new src/anim_eval.rs (document clock `set_document_clock`/`set_app_clock`, start times keyed by node/pseudo/index/name with a Weak node and pruned by `finish_animation_pass` after each build, `TimingFunction::ease`, `directed_progress`, keyframe interval lookup, `lerp_styles`/`merge_styles`, `evaluate`); style.rs: `resolve_style_for` = `resolve_style_core` + `evaluate` only when `animations` is Some (no cost otherwise), keyframe declarations enter the cascade at `ANIM_KEY` (above inline, below !important); css.rs: `transform: none !important` / `translate() !important` no longer dropped (found by css-animations/translation-animation-on-important-property); the WPT runner uses clock 0, the App uses ms since navigation (one evaluation per restyle). Newly passing WPT: 9 (animate-font-size-with-margin-override, animation-delay-011/012, background-color-animation-in-body, important-prop, at-media-content-003, at-supports-content-003, printing/animations-print, pseudo-animations-print). Limits: a property missing from a middle keyframe uses the base value (not the neighbouring keyframe); multiple animations merge only the interpolable fields; keyframe `var()` and CSS-wide keywords ignored; easing is not reversed for reverse/alternate; no frames (QAN1c/d).

## Q30c: checkbox/radio live state (scratchy/q30c-checkbox-radio-state)

**Prompt:** Implement Q30c: live checked/indeterminate state for checkbox and radio (dirty flag over the `checked` attribute, click/Space/label toggling, radio groups per form owner and name, `input`/`change` events, preventDefault restoring the old state, `:checked`/`:indeterminate` on live state, JS `checked`/`indeterminate`/`click()`/`form.reset()`, reset button), with a toggle that does not rebuild the layout tree.

**What changed:** forms.rs holds the state (thread-local `CHECK_LIVE` keyed by `node_id`, not a field on `App`, because selector matching, the JS natives and the painter all run on the main thread without the `App`; entries exist only once dirty; cleared in `replace_document`) plus `set_checked`/`live_checked`/`radio_peers`/`form_owner`/`reset_form_state`. The mark is no longer in the layout tree: `build_checkable` only sets `ComputedStyle::check_widget` (`CHECK_BOX|CHECK_RADIO|CHECK_ATTR`) and `paint::paint_checkable` draws border/fill/check/dot/dash from the live state, so a toggle is a repaint. `:checked`/`:indeterminate` (dom.rs) read the live state and note `STATE_CHECKED`; only pages whose CSS uses them get a restyle on toggle (`App::check_state_changed`, same async path as :hover). `App::click_activate` does legacy pre-activation (toggle, click event, restore on preventDefault, else `input` then `change`, bubbling), label clicks go through it, Space on a focused checkbox/radio activates, reset buttons run `reset_owner_form`. js_dom.rs: natives `__d_checked/__d_setchecked/__d_indet/__d_setindet/__d_radiopeer/__d_resetform`, `checked`/`indeterminate` props, `click()` and `form.reset()` rewritten on them. Tests: 8 `q30c_*`; `q30a_checkbox_and_radio...` and `qy29_data_and_form_props...` were updated to the new design (mark is a style bit; `checked=` no longer sets the attribute). Verified with grim in a nested dwl (fixture: click, label for/wrap, radios in two groups, Space, reset button, checkbox hack, indeterminate; en.wikipedia Vector main-menu checkbox hack opens). Measured toggle-to-present: ~1.5 ms (repaint only, no :checked rules); ~124 ms on en.wikipedia/Test hamburger (restyle path, page uses :checked). Limits: a radio arrow-key group navigation, `cloneNode` copying state, `select`/text state (Q30d/Q30g) not done; Space activates on keydown not keyup.

**Prompt:** Drive CSS animations in the App, settle-first: no in-between frames, one restyle when an animation starts (delay elapsed) and one when it ends, animationstart/iteration/end/cancel as AnimationEvent through App::js_dispatch, next change merged into about_to_wait WaitUntil.

## Q30d: text editing in input/textarea (scratchy/q30d-text-editing)

**Prompt:** Implement Q30d: real text editing in `<input>` (text-like types) and `<textarea>` (live value, caret, selection, clipboard, placeholder, password bullets, maxlength/readonly/disabled, textarea newline/wrap/vertical scroll, mouse caret placement/drag/double click, key events in browser order with page `keydown` winning, `input`/`change` events, JS `value`/`selectionStart/End`/`setSelectionRange`/`select()`), with a keystroke that does not rebuild the layout tree, Esc handing the keys back to scratchy's vim bindings, and `:` typed into social.loupax.com's page vim command line working as text.

**What changed:** new src/forms_text.rs: thread-local `TEXT_LIVE` (node_id -> `TextState` holding a `TextEditBuffer`, dirty flag, placeholder + colour, scroll, value-at-focus), the key handler `App::text_control_key` (pure `Key` input so tests need no winit `KeyEvent`), `edit_text` (beforeinput -> edit -> input), focus hooks (`change` before blur), mouse press/drag/release, clipboard (arboard + internal fallback), shaping/caret/selection/hit-test helpers shared by painter and mouse. Like Q30c, the layout tree no longer holds the text: `build_editable` sets `ComputedStyle::text_widget` and a blank line/`rows` height, and `paint::paint_text_control` shapes the live value (or the placeholder) itself and draws highlight, text and a solid caret, scrolling horizontally (input) or vertically (textarea) to keep the caret visible. `TextEditBuffer` (app.rs) gained an `anchor` and selection/delete/word/line/vertical operations; the command bar behaviour is unchanged. app.rs hooks: KeyboardInput routes to the focused text control after the page's keydown (Tab excepted), `set_focus_element` text focus/blur hooks, Tab selects all, mouse press/drag/release, `clear_text_state` on navigation, `js_key_for`. js_dom.rs: natives `__d_tvalue/__d_settvalue/__d_selget/__d_selset`, `value`/`selectionStart/End/Direction`/`setSelectionRange`/`select` on input and textarea, `keypress` event class, `text_changed` request (repaint only). Tests: 10 `q30d_*` (buffer ops, state/UTF-16/sanitizing, tree has no text, paint of value/placeholder/password/caret/selection/textarea rows, JS round trip, App typing with events/maxlength/readonly/Esc/textarea/clipboard, keydown preventDefault + target); the two `q30a_*` tests that read the value from the layout tree now read what the painter shows. WPT subset: no change. Verified with grim in a nested dwl driven by tools/inject (fixture, wikipedia.org and duckduckgo.com search boxes, social.loupax.com/discover vim line); the portal page screenshot is byte-identical to the previous build when nothing is typed; `--js-report --run-timers 5000` error totals unchanged on all nine pages (0 on wikipedia.org, en.wikipedia Main_Page, news.ycombinator.com). Keystroke-to-present ~8-11 ms on wikipedia.org, ~26-30 ms on duckduckgo.com. Limits (Q30d2/Q30d3): Up/Down by logical line, no undo, no IME preedit, no blink, no textarea wheel scroll, drag selection and cross-app clipboard not verified live.

## QY39b (scratchy/qy39b-user-agent-flag)

**Prompt:** Implement QY39b: a scratchy `--user-agent <string>` flag (and `SCRATCHY_USER_AGENT`) that sets the User-Agent for page loads, sub-resources, fetch/XHR/sendBeacon and media through wire's `X-Wire-User-Agent`, only when wire advertised `X-Wire-Features: ua` (old wire: one warning line, wire's default), validated like wire, with `navigator.userAgent`/`appVersion` agreeing; default unchanged.

**What changed:** new src/user_agent.rs (validation, `UaOverride` with the learn-from-first-response state and the once-only warning, process-wide instance installed at startup by `run`, flag/env resolution, navigator strings). The header is added in the two request builders only (`build_get_request_text_with`, `build_wire_request_with`; any caller-supplied `X-Wire-User-Agent` is dropped so it is sent exactly once); all three response readers (raw, full, media) feed `X-Wire-Features`. `--user-agent` added to dom.rs `parse_args`, `--js-report`, CLI_OPTIONS, help page and README; invalid value is a startup error (exit 1). js.rs prelude reads `userAgent` and `appVersion` (UA minus `Mozilla/`) from the environment; appName/platform unchanged. Real check: own wire + python echo server, page with stylesheet, script, image and fetch: with the flag the echo server logged `x-test/1.0` for /, /s.css, /s.js, /i.png and /f; without it wire's default. Limits: no named presets (skipped, strings go stale); platform not derived from the UA; a set flag is sent on the first request before wire has been seen to support it.

## Q30g: live `<select>` and the dropdown popup (scratchy/q30g-select-popup)
Prompt (coordinator, 2026-11-17): implement Q30g: live selection state for `<select>` (single, `multiple`, `size>1`), JS `value`/`selectedIndex`/`options`/`selectedOptions`/`option.selected`/`add`/`remove`/`length`, input+change events on user change, `defaultSelected`, optgroup + disabled options, `form.reset()`, closed box shows the live selection; a popup overlay (top layer, flips above, scrolls past ~10 rows, min width = select) with hover/click/keyboard/type-ahead/Esc/click-away; listbox click/Ctrl/Shift; `selected_options()` reads the live selection; perf rule: no layout rebuild to open/move/choose.
Done: new src/forms_select.rs (one fn per piece, all colours/sizes in the "look" constants at the top). State: thread-local `SEL_LIVE` keyed by select node id holding the selected options' node ids once dirty (else the `selected` attributes: last `selected` wins for a single select, else the first non-disabled option; a single listbox selects nothing; `multiple` takes every `selected`); a removed selected option falls back to the defaults. `SEL_SNAP` = per-select snapshot (labels, disabled, attribute selection) registered by `forms::build_select` for the painter (no DOM there). The layout tree now only SIZES a select (one blank line, or `size` rows) and carries `ComputedStyle::select_widget` (`SEL_DROP`/`SEL_LIST`); `paint_select_control` draws the live text + chevron / the listbox rows from the live state. `resolve_selection` is the pure rule; `selected_indices`/`set_selected_indices`/`option_is_selected`/`set_option_selected` are the Handle API; `forms_submit::selected_options()` is now `selected_option_handles` (the ONE place). dom.rs `:checked` on `option` uses the live selection; `reset_form_state` also resets selects. JS (js_dom.rs): natives `__d_selidx/__d_setselidx/__d_optsel/__d_setoptsel`; `selectedIndex` and `option.selected` are live, `select.length` has a setter; `value`/`selectedOptions`/`add`/`remove` ride on them. Popup: `App::select_popup` (pure `PopupState`), pure `popup_next_open` (open/close state machine), `popup_key` (Up/Down/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown/Enter/Space/Esc/Tab/type-ahead), `popup_geometry` (below; flips above when there is more room there; shrinks to the room; max 10 rows then scrolls; width = max(select, labels); kept in the window), `popup_hit`; painted in `redraw` after the page and focus ring, before the command bar. Input: an open popup owns every key (Tab closes it then moves focus); a press while open is consumed (choose / ignore header or disabled row / click-away closes) and its release is swallowed (`swallow_release`) so the page never sees it; pointer motion over it highlights the row and gives the page no hover; wheel over it scrolls it. A focused closed select owns the keys like a text control: Space/Enter/F4/Alt-Down open, Up/Down/Left/Right/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown change the selection at once with input+change, letters type-ahead (1 s buffer, a repeated letter cycles), Esc blurs, other keys fall through. Listbox: click selects one, Ctrl-click toggles and Shift-click selects the anchor..clicked range (multiple only, disabled skipped), arrows move/select (Shift extends), Space toggles the cursor option of a multiple. Tests: 11 `q30g_*` (defaults/optgroup/disabled, live selection + `option.selected` + reset, removed option, data set, JS round trips, pure step/type-ahead/click selection, open/close state machine, popup keys, geometry + hit, keyboard events on a closed select, listbox keys); `q30a_select_shows_selected_option...` now reads the painter snapshot instead of layout text. Real checks (nested dwl, tools/inject, grim, all viewed): fixture with single/optgroup/multiple/30-option/bottom selects: click opens the list over the content below with Banana highlighted; hovering Cherry (disabled) does not move the highlight, hovering Apple does; clicking Date closes it, the box shows Date and the page's change handler printed `change:fruit=d idx=3`; the optgroup list shows bold group labels, indented options, grey Okra, Down x3 skips it (Kiwi, Leek, Pea) and Enter chooses; the 30-option list shows 10 rows with a scrollbar, End scrolls to Option number 30, Esc closes with no change and no event; the select near the bottom edge opens ABOVE; with it open, a click on a page button closed the popup and the button's onclick did NOT run; listbox click selected Three (Two cleared), Down moved to Four (change events), "read via JS" printed `value=b sel=Four` (live state through JS), a blurred listbox shows the grey highlight. Real page: https://www.wikipedia.org/ language select (a transparent overlay on the EN label): click shows the language list scrolled to English, clicking Deutsch closed it and the page's own handler changed the label to DE. Open-to-paint latency (temporary Instant timing, removed): Wikipedia portal 118 ms for the first open (cold glyphs), ~50 ms for later opens, 45 ms for choose (includes the page's change handler); no layout rebuild (a restyle is requested only when a stylesheet uses `:checked`). Gates: wikipedia.org, en.wikipedia Main_Page, news.ycombinator.com window screenshots of the new binary vs the installed one are pixel-identical when nothing is clicked (Main_Page differs only in the loading spinner's animation frame); `--js-report --run-timers 5000` on local copies gives the same error counts as the installed binary (2/1/1, all missing relative scripts of a file copy).
Limits: Ctrl/Shift-click could not be injected (tools/inject has no held modifiers), covered by the pure `click_selection` test only; the popup width uses 0.55em per char (no real measuring); no wheel scrolling inside a listbox (the page scrolls); the popup is anchored like the focus ring (ignores inner scroll containers and position:fixed ancestors); no `new Option(...)`; `options.add`/`options.length=` on the collection are not wired (use the select's); an inserted option with a `selected` attribute in an already-dirty select is not selected; page scrolling does not close the popup (it follows the select); Space in an open popup always chooses (no space in type-ahead).

## QY52 (scratchy/qy52-computed-style-cost)

**Prompt:** `getComputedStyle` (`__d_cs`) costs ~50 ms per call after a DOM write on the YouTube results DOM (R37). Measure `style_of` first, then make the QA16 `StyleCache` stop re-cascading on every write; tests for write-then-read freshness, unrelated writes keeping the cache, stylesheet changes invalidating.

**What changed:** js_style.rs `StyleCache`. Measured on YouTube results (3.8 MB CSS, 19k rules): a CSS change re-parsed everything (340-380 ms), the refresh after each write cost 1.5-2 ms, a cold ancestor-chain cascade 4-8 ms; a synthetic 3300-element DOM was only 0.8 ms per write+read, so the cost is the rules, not the DOM. (1) The rule list is now per stylesheet piece (each `<style>`, the external CSS, the adopted CSS, the last two keyed by a version counter) and only changed pieces are re-parsed and spliced in (pages using `@layer` keep the old joined parse). (2) Cached styles carry a fingerprint (attributes and `:empty`-ness of the element, sibling tags, earlier siblings' attributes only when some selector uses `+`/`~`/`:nth-child(of)`, viewport, interaction state) cumulated down the ancestor chain, so a write elsewhere no longer invalidates them; `:has(` rules and form controls fall back to the write generation. images.rs `collect_style_pieces`. Tests qy52_get_computed_style_reflects_every_kind_of_write and qy52_unrelated_writes_keep_cached_styles_and_stylesheets_invalidate (cascade/parse counters as a test seam). YouTube after: __d_cs 1.1-3.4 ms per call after writes, 23-30 ms on a stylesheet change (was 350 ms).

**Prompt:** IntersectionObserver built its rects from the `width`/`height` attributes (0x0 for YouTube's lazy `<img>`s, so lazy loaders dropped them) and reported each target once. ## QY53o3b: cheaper shape-memo keys (scratchy/qy53o3b-cheap-memo-keys, Sonnet)

**Prompt:** Implement QY53o3b: with a warm memo `measure_document` still spends ~21 % in SipHash (`memo_key`), ~14 % in memmove (`to_string` copies made only to build keys) and ~5 % in `Instant::now` deadline checks. The key stays 64 bits (same exposure as the old SipHash-64 key); no stored full key. ## QYSK1a: hold the old MSE generation while an out-of-buffer seek waits (Sonnet)

> Do TODO.txt item QYSK1a (R51 section 4, in PR #375): when an MSE seek targets a time outside the buffered data, MediaCore only stores `want` and mpv keeps playing the old generation, which YouTube's `play()` then unpauses. Add a `hold` flag on `MseAttach` + `backend.set_paused(true)` while the seek waits; play/pause do not touch the backend while held; the old generation's Time/Eof/Buffering events are ignored; `mse_resolve` clears it. FakeBackend test + real-mpv test. Not QYSK1b.

**What changed:** media_el.rs: `MseAttach.hold`, set in `mse_seek` when the target is neither in the live generation nor covered; `start_playing`/`pause` skip the backend while held (element state and events unchanged); `handle` drops Time/Eof/Buffering/Restart while held (Restart too: a late one would end `seeking` early); `mse_resolve` clears it on the in-generation path (`seek` then `set_paused(self.paused)`) and before the new-generation load (which already applies `paused`). Detach/reset drop the attachment, so the hold goes with it; endOfStream leaves it (the backend stays paused until data covers the target). Tests: two `qysk1a_*` in mse_tests/qm1k1c.rs (FakeBackend), real-mpv `qysk1a_out_of_buffer_seek_holds_old_generation_then_resumes_at_target` in mse_mpv_tests.rs (spy backend records raw mpv Time events).

## QSTASH-D: persistent storage design, STASH.md (design session, docs only)

The prompts of the design session, in order:

> I've been thinking, we'll need some persistance soon in scratchy. history, local storage, things like that. I wonder if we can have the store external similarly to how we do with wire. I can have an "in memory" store that persists changes between scratchy sessions, and I can give it commands to have it store data to the disk later. give me a critical review of such a feature

> I agree with the overall design, but I don't like how wire becomes an "everything io" tool

> try and show me how this daemon will work. paint me a picture during a browsing session

> first of all, like the name stash. second, any specific reason we use HTTP vocabulary?

> we got the design of wire for free because it's basically an http client. I want to think about stash a bit more. Initially I was thinking of being able to have an in-memory version of stash, an HDD backed version, maybe an s3 version later all in separate binaries. Or even if we keep a single binary this design choice will force our design to be extendable. On the other hand storing data is basically "writing to disk". Maybe we could mimic the "everything is a file" philosophy of linux and lean on the existing file io interface. how would an interface needed by scratchy look like?

> I agree using the FS as an absraction is likely the best solution for this. Is the netstring still necessary? what problem does it solve?

> what will happen if I open a WTF-8 encoded file in nvim and make changes to it? will parsing break?

> regarding data races. Can we introduce a locking system between scratchy instances?

> do it in a PR so I can review it first

**What changed:** docs only. New `STASH.md` (no daemon; `--state-dir` with one file per localStorage key, WTF-8 values with a one-trailing-newline rule, per-site flock with a generation number, sessionStorage never on disk, wire keeps the jar with `--cookie-file`, history deferred). TODO.txt: decision QSTASH-D, items QSTASH1-QSTASH5, a queue note (after the perf queue), QF-D7 marked superseded for these stores. wire/TODO.txt: W-PERSIST1.

## QPT1 (design): a same-origin iframe gets its own V8 realm (Opus, docs only)

> Item QPT1, DESIGN step (docs only). The user approved QPT1 ahead of the performance queue ("ok, lets do what Chrome does then"): a same-origin iframe gets its own JS realm = a new V8 context in the same isolate and on the same thread, with its own built-ins, and `contentWindow`/`document.defaultView` is that context's global. Design it from the source (main context, snapshot, preludes and natives per document, the iframe's second document, contentWindow/parent/top/frameElement/frames/postMessage, scripts in srcdoc/about:blank, lifetime, cross-realm identity, timers/microtasks, memory per context), compare with Chrome, write a REGRESSIONS.md entry with risks and an ordered split QPT1a.. (S/M each; the first is the smallest slice that gives BotGuard its built-ins, checked against R52), plus this entry. No product code.

**What changed:** docs only. REGRESSIONS.md R53 has the design D1-D9 (a context from snapshot context 0 in the page isolate with a shared security token; a baked `__scratchy_realm_init` hook binds the document id, frame links and env; the realm's host queues forward to the parent's; lifetime/cap; one wrapper per node across realms; the WindowProxy surface; scripts in same-origin iframes), the risks, and the split QPT1a (BotGuard slice, M) to QPT1f, plus QPT1g as backlog. A throwaway spike (not committed) measured ~1.2-1.5 ms and ~0.65 MB of V8 heap per realm, all of it freed after the references are dropped. Without a shared token `w.String` throws `no access`. The baked realm document is the page's (id 0), the realm's timers never fire and its rejections are lost: D2/D5 fix those three. One question for the user: `data:` iframes (Chrome makes them opaque-origin).

## QM1g2a: render libmpv video frames off the main thread (Opus)

> Item QM1g2a [M] (P2 perf): render libmpv video frames off the main thread. A worker thread that owns the mpv render context (created, updated and freed on one thread), renders into a buffer the main thread presents (latest-frame slot, no tearing, no stale frame after seek/resize/element removal), wakeups via mpv's update callback, clean shutdown when the element goes away. Keep the QM1k1n6c damage-present path. Unit tests for the frame slot / lifecycle, a real-mpv test that frames arrive from the worker; measure main-thread ms per video frame, fps and input latency before/after in a nested dwl (local fixture and YouTube G1AeBgalFZk) under the perf flock.

**What changed:** new `media_render.rs` (`RenderWorker`: thread `scratchy-video`, `FrameRenderer` trait built and dropped on the worker, one-frame slot, an epoch bumped by target change/seek/load/unload so a stale frame is never published, redraw of the current frame on resize, join on drop). `media_mpv.rs`: `MpvRenderer` (the `sw` render context) lives on the worker; `take_frame`/`frame_pending` only read the slot; `drop` joins the worker before `mpv_terminate_destroy`. Frame stats gain `video.tick_ms`/`video.fetch_ms`. Tests: `media_render_tests.rs` (stub renderer), real-mpv `qm1g2a_mpv_frames_arrive_from_the_render_worker` (media_tests.rs). Measurements: REGRESSIONS.md R46 "QM1g2a" (main-thread ms per frame 4.1-5.9 -> 1.0-1.2 local, 8.5-10.0 -> 2.2-2.4 YouTube).

## QPT1c: cross-realm wrapper identity (Opus)

> Item QPT1c [M]: R53 D7, Chrome's rule: one JS wrapper per DOM node across all realms of a page, made by (and with the prototypes of) the realm that owns the node's document. `f.contentDocument.body` from the parent and `document.body` in the realm are the same object, `instanceof f.contentWindow.HTMLElement` true and `instanceof HTMLElement` false; a node moved between documents keeps its identity (and its creation realm's prototype); dropped realms leave no dangling wrappers. Live gate: YouTube still gets a token.

**What changed:** js_dom.rs DOM prelude: `wrap` split into `wrap` (cache, then owner-realm delegation) and `mk` (makes the wrapper in this realm); the page-wide `cache`, `owners` and realm table `xr` (`byDoc`: document id -> owner realm's `mk`, `n`: live iframe realms) passed in `realm_init` (`o.dom`) and switched to in `__d_bind_doc`; new native `__d_root(id)` (tree root); a removed node records the document it left while realms exist, an inserted node with a recorded owner gets the new document, `document.adoptNode` records the adopter instead of forgetting it; `__d_realm_purge` (called by `__scratchy_realm_release`) deletes a dropped realm's wrappers still in its documents (or detached), its documents and the `owners` entries naming them. Chrome: Blink keeps the wrapper (and so its prototype) of a node adopted into another document; scratchy does the same (Firefox swaps the prototype). Tests `qpt1c_*` in js_dom_tests.rs; NOTES.md "iframe realms". MutationObserver registries stay per realm (an observer sees the mutations made through its own realm's DOM methods).

## QY53e2: IntersectionObserver uses the App's own layout in a window (Sonnet)

> Do TODO.txt item QY53e2 (perf queue step 15): in a window, IntersectionObserver evaluates on the App's own complete layout instead of forcing one; keep the forced path for headless and for a stale App layout. Gate: nested dwl, own wire, Wikipedia and YouTube, under flock, counts of forced layouts by caller IO.

**What changed:** `App::redraw` records `js_geom::render_stamp()` (geometry generation + in-place shifts, CSS versions) when it builds a tree; on a COMPLETE current `ShapeResult` `handle_shape_result` calls `JsEngine::rendered_geometry(&laid, stamp, w, h)`. It does nothing unless the stamp still equals the page as it is now and a deferred IO recheck is waiting (`__scratchy_ioWant`); then `js_geom::set_rendered` keeps a read-only rect map of the Laid (thread-local, `walk()` + the shared `find_in` fallbacks) and `__scratchy_ioRendered` runs the recheck with `gRend` on (`__d_rect_r`, validated by `__d_rend_ok` against stamp and viewport, cleared after the flush and by a new engine). The QY53e1 deadline is unchanged in a window (coordinator: a flat 2 s window deadline was tried and dropped: up to 2 s late IO delivery is not worth the saved forced layouts). Tests: same entries from App layout and forced layout (clipped, scrolled-container, fixed, transformed, display:none, inline targets), stale layout forces, new engine drops it, window with no App layout forces at the normal deadline.

## QMEM3j: SHAPE_MEMO hit rate vs bytes, then cap or sweep it (Opus; answers QY53o3c too; 80d5353)

> Item QMEM3j [S] (P2 memory; measure, then the fix). Measure SHAPE_MEMO (JS-thread and App/worker memos) hit rate vs bytes on Wikipedia and YouTube (headless --perf-report and a live nested-window run, own wire/socket); then cap or sweep it so memory drops substantially without losing the hits that matter (e.g. byte budget with LRU/generation sweep, or storing a compact shaped form instead of the full cosmic-text Buffer). Gate: Wikipedia RSS/malloc in_use clearly lower (state the number), forced-layout and App build times not worse (interleaved before/after runs under the perf flock). Tests: cap respected; memo still hits on repeated layouts of the same page; no visual change (a layout fixture compares rects). Also answer QY53o3c (unbounded growth on a long-lived page?) if it falls out of the same work.

**What changed:** measured first (REGRESSIONS.md R48 "QMEM3j"): 89 % (JS thread) to 97-99 % (worker) of lookups hit and nearly every entry is reused each layout, so a cap would only lose hits; instead each entry got smaller. layout.rs: `shape_spans` uses the first span's attrs as the cosmic-text line default (a one-span line keeps no 1.5 KB attribute B-tree leaf) and shrinks `Buffer::lines`; `memo_put` swaps a new entry's buffer for its clone (exact capacities: cosmic-text reserves the span list per byte and grows glyph vectors by doubling). Wikipedia memo 69.6 -> 31.4 MB, malloc in_use 107.5 -> 69.2 MB, RSS 281 -> 243.5 MB headless and -55..-78 MB in a window; forced layouts and App builds not slower. `shape_memo_mem` now sums the public capacities (29.5 vs 31.4 MB real) and the report has `memory.shape_memo_lookups`. QY53o3c: yes, the worker memo grew ~3 KB/s on YouTube (cleared only on non-restyle rebuilds); `memo_sweep(cap, keep)` gained a pass age, and the worker sweeps after each finished build keeping what the last 8 builds used (`memo_clear` clears the age map too). Tests: `shape_memo_tests.rs` (fixture layout identical with fresh, stored and memo-hit shapes, no capacity slack, first-span defaults shape like the old ones, sweep keep/cap policy).

> Item QPT1d [S]: R53 D8, the WindowProxy surface of same-origin iframe realms: `frames`, `length`, `window[i]`, `window[name]`, cross-realm `postMessage` (target realm's clone and MessageEvent, sender window as `source`, targetOrigin respected), `closed`, `name`.

**What changed:** js_dom.rs `syncWin` (child list getters, document order, lazy windows counted); js.rs page/realm `name` and `closed`; globals_prelude.js `postMessage` (incumbent source/origin, closed target drops); js_engine_v8.rs natives `__scratchy_incumbent` and `__scratchy_enter`, and `DetachGlobal` removed (stale `w.closed` must read true). Tests `qpt1d_*` in js_dom_tests.rs.

> Item QPT1d3 [XS]: timers and requests created on a CLOSED window (iframe removed, `w.closed` true) must do nothing (Chrome).

**What changed:** js.rs timers prelude: a realm `add` returns an id without queueing when `g.closed` (covers setTimeout/setInterval/rAF/rIC). fetch_prelude.js `__net_fwd`: a closed realm`s `__net_request` sends nothing: async/fetch gets a never-settling promise (same as QPT1b cancelled requests), sync XHR throws NetworkError. Test `qpt1d3_*` in js_dom_tests.rs.

## QYTC1b: a write that restores an attribute to its layout-time value cancels its geometry bump (Sonnet)

> Item QYTC1b [S] (P2, from R50): `ytp-autohide-active` added and removed between two reads forced a layout that changes no box (11-13 % of YouTube's controls-visible forced layouts).

**Not merged (docs only):** measured no effect after QYTC1a; code on branch `scratchy/qytc1b-ledger-code`.

**What changed (on that branch):** js_geom.rs `GeomCache::ledger` (`AttrLedger`) + `attr_write_bumped`: every attribute write through `__d_setattr/__d_rmattr/__d_setq/__d_rmq` that bumps the geometry generation is recorded (node, name, value at layout time, current value) while the cache is the current layout; the ledger is exact only while every bump since the layout came from a recorded write (`expected` generation) and the CSS version is unchanged, otherwise it is dropped (next layout re-anchors). When all recorded attributes equal their layout-time value again the cache key is rebased onto the new generation (the generation still moves, so other caches stay conservative; HIDDEN/ATTR_SNAP are rebased too). js_dom.rs `geom_bump_attr_tracked`. Any other bump (insert/remove, innerHTML, text, sheet, style non-in-place, setns) poisons it. Tests `qytc1b_*` in js_geometry_tests.rs.


> Item QFLK2 [S]: `qy53e2_app_layout_gives_the_same_entries_as_a_forced_layout_without_forcing` failed in full runs (2 of 2 seen), passes alone.

**What changed:** root cause: the IO recheck deadline in js_dom.rs `__scratchy_ioTick` is `min(2000, max(100, 4 x __d_geom_cost()))` where the cost is the MEASURED thread-CPU time of the last forced layout (`GeomCache::last_cost_ms`); in a parallel full run (contended caches/CPU) the initial layout cost more than 25 ms, the deadline moved to 170 ms instead of 150 and the test's exact `150 far true` line failed. Nothing is shared between tests (RENDERED, GEOM_GEN, CSS_VER are all thread-local). Fix: `js_geom::TEST_FIXED_COST_MS` (cfg(test) thread-local) pins the cost to 1 ms; set in `qy53e2_run`, `qy53e1_run` and `qy57_run`, so every test that asserts delivery times is immune. Product code unchanged.

## QY53n2: paint-only hover patch (Opus)

> Do TODO.txt item QY53n2: per-rule effect class (PAINT/OFFSET/LAYOUT) in RuleDerived; a hover change whose affected elements only gain/lose PAINT-class rules re-resolves those elements, patches the installed Laid tree and the affected paragraphs' span attrs, and repaints (no build, no shaping); everything else builds as today; frame stats `hover.patched`. Also settle QHOV1 (no hover underline on Wikipedia links?).

New `hover_patch.rs` `paint_patch`: resolves the affected elements (changed + element descendants, and their before/after) down their ancestor chains with the kept memo under the old and the new state; the old values must equal what the `Laid` boxes and spans hold, the new values are written (boxes in place; paragraphs as re-laid copies in the App's shape cache, never the worker's memo entry); updates the kept memo; any doubt -> `Err` with nothing changed -> build as before. `App::apply_hover` tries it when the diff is non-empty and no layout is in flight.
