**Measured** (Wikipedia Rust `--no-js`, nested dwl, own wire, 8 links = 5 TOC entries + Talk/Edit/View history, 6 rounds x 600 ms, under flock): branch 4.3 / 7.3 / 7.4 ms of builds per hover_restyle (median 7.3; the only builds are the page load's 3-4), hover.patched 49 of 49 in each run (100 %), 3.9-9.9 ms per patch; main at load 3-4: 144 ms per hover_restyle (51 of 51 built). Hovered-link and hovered-tab screenshots pixel-identical to main's. QHOV1: the underline DOES paint on main (pointer held 1.5 s, screenshot after the frame): the TOC link is underlined in main's and the branch's screenshots. After the rebase on QMEM3j (first span = line default attrs; the patch now rewrites defaults too): 100 % patched in 3 runs at load 25-37, builds per hover_restyle 10.6 / 5.5 / 26.7 ms, screenshots equal main's.
## QY53f1d: YouTube's cold 4.4 MB stylesheet parse: measure, design, first slice (Opus; 622b2c3)

> Item QY53f1d [M] (P3 perf; measure first, then design + the first slice). The cold parse of YouTube's 4.4 MB stylesheet still costs ~130 ms on the first forced layout (and the App's first build). Write the design + items in REGRESSIONS.md and implement the first slice if it is <= M and sound.

**What changed:** measured (REGRESSIONS.md R54): since QY53f1c the cold parse is 34-55 ms quiet (tokenizer ~55 %, selectors ~35 %; declarations are lazy) and runs in the first getComputedStyle, but YouTube re-parsed the whole sheet 3-4 more times per minute: QYTC1a's `IMP_GEO` in js_geom.rs held a clone of the rule list's `Rc`, so every `<style>` insert fell back from QY53f1's splice to a full parse. The `!important` geometry cache now keeps the matching rules' selector lists and the `rules_cache` generation instead of the `Rc`. Design for the rest: worker-thread parse of the external CSS (QY53f1d1), one RuleIndex per rule list (QY53f1d2), incremental derived data on splice (QY53f1d3); lazy selector parsing rejected (saves <= 13 ms for an L change).

## QYTC1d: a class write that changes no element's matched rules keeps the forced layout (Opus)

> Item QYTC1d [S/M] (P3, from QYTC1b #404 R50): after QYTC1a, YouTube's remaining controls layouts start from a stale cache (progress-bar style, aria and player `class` writes); let the in-place path and reads proceed when the cache is stale only because of writes that are provably box-neutral (write ledger; unread attributes, in-place shifts, class writes whose matched-rule set is unchanged). Exactness first.

**What changed:** no ledger: a provably inert write simply does not bump the geometry generation, so the cache stays the current layout and QYTC1a's in-place path and QY53o1's unread-attribute skip keep applying after it (aria writes were already inert while the cache was current). New: js_geom.rs `class_write_pre`/`class_write_post` + `ClassDeps` (per `rules_cache` generation, selector clones, never the rule list's `Rc` (QY53f1d)): around a `class` write in `__d_setattr`/`__d_rmattr`, the selectors of the rules naming a changed class plus those reading `class` as an attribute are matched against every element the change can reach, before and after; equal = inert. A `:has()`/`:nth-child(of)` class (not parsed today), `content: attr(class)`, > 20 000 matches, or a stale cache: bump as before. Tests `qytc1d_*` in js_geometry_tests.rs; two older tests now use a class some rule names.

**Measured:** R50 recipe at 960x1006 (the nested window size), 3 interleaved pairs under the perf flock, load 9-25: controls-phase forced layouts 11-13 -> 9-12 per run, whole run 0-3 fewer; the remaining ~1/s is the time display's text-node replacement. REGRESSIONS.md R50 "QYTC1d result".

## QY47b: fewer JS frames per createElement (Sonnet, measure first)

Ship the fold of the media check into the DOM prelude only if it saves something measurable; otherwise a docs-only PR recording "no measurable saving, close QY47b".

One extra identical wrapper costs +82..+105 ns per `createElement("div")` (1M calls: ~1000 ms vs ~1090 ms, 4 interleaved pairs under flock, load 0.4); that is ~2.5 ms at most on a YouTube results load, and the QuickJS-era stack-depth motivation does not apply to V8. ## QY54a design: keep reading the Wayland socket while the main thread is busy (Opus)

> Coordinator: design step of QY54a (docs only). The nested dwl disconnects scratchy once ~190-225 pointer-motion events sit unread (R56 QY54: a 450 ms busy loop at 500 Hz is enough), whatever blocks the main thread; no budget can fix it. Study how scratchy uses winit/softbuffer and the Wayland connection; weigh a helper thread doing prepare_read/read_events, moving JS+layout off the winit thread, pumping from long work, coalescing; feasibility with the current crates, invasiveness, risk, input order and hit-testing. A throwaway prototype is welcome. Recommend one, split into sized items with gates (overall gate: busy450 and stall_k18 at 500 Hz survive 3/3 with the R56 recipe). One docs PR: R-section + this entry.

**What changed:** REGRESSIONS.md R57 only (no code; the prototype lived in the scratchpad and was never committed). Recommendation: a `wl-drain` helper thread that reads (never dispatches) a second `wayland_client::Connection` made from winit's `wl_display*` (`Backend::from_foreign_display`; winit 0.30.13 runs on system libwayland 1.26, which supports several readers). Events still land in winit's queue in socket order and only the main thread dispatches, so input order and hit-testing do not change. Prototype (winit 0.30.13 + softbuffer 0.4.8, built offline against scratchy's Cargo.lock, nested dwl, ~460 Hz inject circle): without the thread a 450 ms and a 3 s busy loop are lost at the first stall; with it 3/3 + 3/3 survive, no move is lost, the order is kept, cost +0.08 s sys CPU per 15 s of motion; it must stop at the first error (it logged extra `Broken pipe` lines when the compositor died). Rejected: a separate UI thread (XL), checkpoints in long work (one per stall kind), aborting work, bigger buffers (server-side limit). Proposed QY54a1 (stall harness in tools/wl-flood, S), QY54a2 (the drain thread, M), QY54a3 (YouTube + CPU re-measure, S).

> Coordinator: TODO.txt QY53n1c (R55, QY53n2c note #424): about a third of the YouTube watch hover restyles that still build do so because `hover_match_diff` returns None, the kept match memo being for an old rule list after a QY53f1 `<style>` splice. ## QY54b3 design: lay out less than the whole page for a script geometry read (Opus, design only, docs only)

> Coordinator: design step of QY54b3 (absorbs QY53o2). Design a subtree forced layout for the JS thread's GeomCache: which boxes qualify as a layout boundary, how the subtree is styled (parent's cached style, inherited and custom properties, ancestor/sibling selectors), measuring at the cached containing block, splicing rects/skeleton/glyphs, hoisted abs/fixed descendants, IO reads, counters/::before order (QY54b2), fall-back conditions, and an exactness test mode (tests + an env var on real pages). Estimate the win on the R58 recipe, split into S/M items with gates (overall: gPS layouts median < 10 ms, worst preview-start promise job < 300 ms), say if it is too risky or not worth it. One docs PR: R-section + this entry.

**What changed:** REGRESSIONS.md R59 only (no code; a throwaway prototype test lived in the scratchpad for one debug run and was removed). Recommendation: go, in two stages that share the dirty-point tracking (where each geometry write landed) and a stash from the last full layout (parent `InheritedStyle`, own `ComputedStyle`, containing-block size per candidate box). Stage 1 answers `getBoundingClientRect`/`offset*` of an "insulating" box (own formatting context, size not from content, block-formatted) or of anything outside it from the stale cache with no layout, when every write is inside that box. Stage 2 re-builds and measures only the nearest abs/fixed insulating box at a provisional origin with its stashed containing-block size, translates it to its cached place and splices rects, skeleton and glyphs. Both run under a check mode (always in tests, `SCRATCHY_GEOM_CHECK=1` on real pages). Prototype: an R58-like wrapper built alone from its parent's inherited style and measured at (0, 0), then translated, equals the full layout to 0.00024 px over 13 boxes. Estimate: stage 1 alone serves ~55-70 % of gPS reads at ~0 ms (needs QY54b1's player CSS), worst job ~255-550 ms; stages 1+2 ~190-330 ms. Proposed QY54b3a (classifier, go/no-go, M), QY54b3b (stage 1, M), QY54b3c (counter state per abs box, S), QY54b3d (subtree build, M), QY54b3e (measure + splice, overall gate, M), QY54b3f (real-page check sweep + QY53o2 gate, S).

## QFLK3: qb2_js_dom_writes_use_restyle_path fails alone (Sonnet)

> Fix TODO item QFLK3: tests::js_dom_tests::qb2_js_dom_writes_use_restyle_path fails intermittently, also on main when run alone ("stale-promise" assertion; `done` undefined, expected "AAA"). Find the order/timing dependence (shared thread-locals/statics, wall-clock timers, microtask ordering, IO deadlines) and make it deterministic. The script of `qf7_app_net` was built from `qf7_go`, whose own `.then` already calls `r.text()` (to log `ok ...`); the test then chained a second `r.text()` on the same Response, which rejects with "body already used" (stderr: `js error: Uncaught (in promise) TypeError ... body already used`), so `window.__done` was never set and `done()` stayed "undefined". `qf7_go` gained that consuming chain after the test was written. ## QINC1 design: proper incremental style + layout, in one go (Opus, design only, docs only)

> Coordinator (user, 2026-11-20: "can we focus on doing incremental layout properly in one go?"): design how real browsers do it, adapted to scratchy (JS geometry cache vs the App's rendered layout, V8, winit main thread): a persistent box/fragment tree, per-node dirty bits from every kind of write, selector invalidation sets, incremental restyle with inherited propagation and early cut-off, relayout of dirty subtrees with boundaries and intrinsic caches, fragment caching, paint invalidation. Decide one engine or two, fold in the special cases (QYTC1a/d, QY53m, QY53n, MATCH_MEMO/HoverKeys/RuleDerived, QY53f1, QY54b1, R59), a correctness strategy (verify mode in tests, env var, kill switch, WPT), a migration path that keeps main green, estimates for YouTube results gPS, YouTube watch, Wikipedia and App builds, an honest size/risk; one docs PR with a new R-section, sized ordered items with areas for 5 parallel agents, and open questions.

**What changed:** REGRESSIONS.md R60 only (no code). A throwaway probe in the scratchpad (never committed) compared every forced layout's styles, DOM and rects with the previous one on YouTube results/watch and Wikipedia (headless, own wire, flock): the median layout restyles 3-33 elements of 261-1 128 styled ones (1-5 %) and touches 1-6 % of the boxes, while today every layout redoes all of it. Recommendation: ONE engine on the main thread for App frames and script forced layouts (they already share the thread and the `Rc` DOM): an element table with a match cache and stored styles, an `InvalidationMap` generalizing ClassDeps/HoverKeys/AttrReaders, top-down restyle with early cut-off and an exhaustive `style_diff`, the `LayoutBox` tree kept and rebuilt per container, the last `Laid` tree as the fragment cache (constraint keys, harvest of clean subtrees, bottom-up re-measure that stops when the parent-visible result is unchanged), stable paragraph ids, bottom-up hoisting. Shadow mode compares it with the from-scratch path in every test from the first stage, plus a differential fuzzer; `SCRATCHY_INCR_CHECK=1` on real pages; `SCRATCHY_INCR=0` kill switch. 14 items QINC1a-QINC1m (4 L) in 5 waves; projected `getPlayerSize` 54-80 ms -> ~2-5 ms and App builds 38-90 ms -> ~2-6 ms. Supersedes R59/QY54b3a-f and ~12 narrow items.

> Implement TODO item QPT1b2 (R53 D6): WebSockets created in a dropped iframe realm use the parent's class and stay open until they close on their own. ## QYSCR1: scrolling does not work on YouTube (Opus, user bug)

> Coordinator: TODO.txt QYSCR1 (user 2026-11-20: "scrolling doesn't work on youtube in general"). Reproduce wheel / keyboard (Space, PageDown, Down) on YouTube home, results and watch in a nested window with grim before/after. Suspect: body `overflow: scroll` with a 0 px box (R56) used as the scroll container instead of the viewport (QY57r fixed only IntersectionObserver); also check hit_test_scroll_region, ytd-app / fixed containers, JS wheel handlers, window.scrollTo, page height. **What changed:** three causes (REGRESSIONS.md R61). images.rs `propagate_viewport_overflow` applies CSS Overflow 3 viewport propagation once per layout-tree build (App and GeomCache): `<html>`'s, else `<body>`'s, `overflow` becomes `visible` on that element, so it is no scroll region, no clip and no stacking boundary (`VIEWPORT_ROOT_NODE` removed); `contain: layout/paint/strict/content` (new `ComputedStyle::contain_lp`) stops the body propagation. js_dom.rs `gViewportBody` is the same rule for `gScrollable` and `ioEval0`. layout.rs `in_flow_bottom` counts absolute boxes, so a page held in YouTube's absolute `ytd-app` gets its real height. app.rs: `region_takes_wheel` hands a tick the region under the cursor cannot use to the page; Space/PageDown/PageUp/Shift+Space/arrows scroll. Tests: 8 `qyscr1_*` in interaction_tests.rs. WPT: 12 more overflow-body-propagation reftests in the subset, 001/005/006/010 newly pass. Real check: YouTube results and watch scroll by wheel, PageDown and Down (comments and related reached); Wikipedia and HN unchanged. Left out: QYSCR1a-d (R61).

## QNAV9a+b: `scratchy file:///path` opens the file; relative file links work without wire (Sonnet)

> Implement QNAV9a and QNAV9b (one PR): (a) `scratchy file:///abs/path.html` must open the file (classify_input accepts file:// via Url::to_file_path; percent-encoded paths; non-local hosts rejected with a clear error). (b) Without --socket a file page gets base_url from file_page_url, so relative hrefs resolve and #frag scrolls; following a relative file link without wire should load the local file or give a clear message; no network access added.

**What changed:** `classify_input` (dom.rs) turns a `file://` URL into `Input::File(<decoded local path>)` (`%20` etc. decoded, `localhost` accepted); `parse_args` first calls the new `file_url_error` and exits with a clear message for `file://host/...` (other host) or a path-less URL. A statically opened file with no `--socket` now gets `base_url = file_page_url(path)` (lib.rs), so relative hrefs resolve and `#frag` scrolls. `fetch_url_inner` (app.rs) with no socket and a `file:` URL calls the new `read_local_file_page` (net.rs): reads the file from disk (no network, no wire), picks html / text / image wrapping by extension (unknown = html), no sub-resources (stylesheets, images and external scripts need wire); inline scripts still run (`handle_nav_result`). With `--socket`, `file:` links still go through wire as before. Missing files give "cannot open <path>: <io error>" on the message page. Tests: `qnav9a_file_url_argument_opens_the_local_path`, `qnav9b_without_wire_a_relative_file_link_loads_the_local_file`. Real check in a nested dwl on a page in a directory with a space (`file:///.../dir%20with%20space/index.html`), with and without `--socket` (own wire): the `#frag` link scrolls to the anchor, the relative link loads `two.html`.

## QYSCR1b + QYSCR1c: hidden viewport overflow and scroll chaining (Sonnet, coordinator items)

> Coordinator: TODO.txt QYSCR1b (viewport `overflow: hidden`, e.g. YouTube body.no-scroll while a dialog is open, blocks wheel/key scrolling but not window.scrollTo/scrollBy/scrollIntoView; same for element regions with overflow:hidden) and QYSCR1c (a wheel tick an inner region cannot use goes to the next scrollable ancestor, then the viewport; a region with nothing to scroll does not swallow the tick; keys follow the same chain if scratchy has a focused/clicked scroll region, else the viewport). Tests, nested-dwl check with a local fixture and YouTube watch, R61 note.

**What changed:** images.rs `propagate_viewport_overflow` records a propagated `hidden` on the root box (`Style::viewport_hidden`); app.rs `viewport_user_scroll_blocked` makes the wheel's page fallback and all scroll actions (j/k, arrows, Space, PageUp/Down, Home/End, gg/G, half pages) do nothing, while script scrolling (`scroll_offset` from `scrollTo`/`scrollIntoView`) is untouched. layout.rs `make_scroll_info` also makes `overflow: hidden` boxes scroll regions with `ScrollInfo::user == false` (no scrollbar, never a wheel target, no ink shift), and js_dom.rs `gScrollable` accepts `hidden`, so `scrollTop`/`scrollIntoView` work on them (qj6 test updated: a hidden box now keeps `scrollTop = 20`). paint.rs `hit_test_scroll_chain` lists every region under the cursor innermost first; the wheel takes the first user region that can move in that direction, then the page. Keys have no focused scroll region in scratchy, so they stay on the viewport. Tests: 4 `qyscr1b/c_*` in interaction_tests.rs. Real check (nested dwl, local fixture with nested scroll boxes, a hidden box, a fits-box and a body.overflow toggle; YouTube watch): inner scroll box scrolls to its end, then the outer takes the ticks; over a hidden box the outer takes them; with body overflow hidden wheel, PageDown, Down, Space leave the page at y=80 while scrollTo(0,300), scrollIntoView and a hidden box's scrollTop still move; toggling back restores the wheel. YouTube dialog not reachable logged out. Left out: scroll regions that are absolutely positioned are still not wheel targets (existing cut in `hit_test_scroll_region`).

## QOOM1: 15 GB scratchy OOM: removed <video> elements kept their players (Opus, coordinator assignment)

> Investigate and fix TODO item QOOM1 (P1): a scratchy reached 15 GB anon RSS and was OOM-killed; headless `--perf-report` runs hit the 6 GB cap in 26-33 s with `dav1d-worker` triggering the OOM. Reproduce headless under a cap with RSS sampled every second, bisect what grows (memprof, V8 heap, mpv/libdav1d, render thread, frame pool, wire buffering), fix the root cause, regression test for the bounded structure, verify 5 min headless + 20 min nested window on YouTube watch, R-section, PR.

**What changed:** the page is the github.com home: its hero section is re-rendered about once a second, each time inserting two new `<video>` elements (AV1 + HEVC, ~250 MB per libmpv player with 16 decoder threads) and removing the old ones. A removed media element was only paused; `__media_drop` existed but nothing called it, so every player lived until the page went away (14 players / 3.8 GB at 7 s). media_prelude.js: when the removal's MutationObserver record is delivered and the element is still out of the document, it is paused and its core dropped (`__media_drop`); it stays inert (never loads, `play()` rejects) until it is put back, when it loads again. media_el.rs `MediaHost`: dropped ids get a throwaway inert core (no backend) until `revive`; a dropped player asks for `malloc_trim` (at most once a second; glibc kept 1.86 GB free in its arenas). Tests `qoom1_*` in media_tests.rs. REGRESSIONS.md R63.

## QINC1f-fix: incremental-restyle mismatches the 3 000-case fuzz found (R60; agent item, no behaviour change)

> Fix TODO item QINC1f-fix: the QINC1g agent's 3 000-case fuzz run found 7 STYLE mismatches in QINC1f's incremental restyle (seeds 462, 519, 733, 1956, 2080, 2084, 2475; `:first-child` / `:nth-child` / `+` / `~` after inserts and moves). Find each root cause (InvalidationMap's for_children reach, how moves are reported, the write log's sibling info), fix it soundly (over-marking is fine), add each seed's minimal reproducer as a named test, make it hard to regress (fixed seeds or a larger default count in CI, report the runtime). Gate: 0 style and box mismatches over 5 000 cases across at least 3 seeds.

**What changed:** two causes. (1) All seven seeds: the log is replayed against the FINAL DOM, and `for_children`'s structural edges ("first two / last two element children", the element after the change point) were computed per entry there; a batch that inserts several elements in front of the old first child (a parsed fragment goes in one node at a time) left the old first child third, so it kept `div:first-child` (same for appends and `:last-child`). New `InvalidationMap::for_child_list(parent, old)` compares the parent's element children at the last restyle (its stored child keys that have entries, captured before the log is processed) with the current ones: old and new first/last (`:first/last/only-child`), every element whose previous element sibling changed (`+`), every element from the first difference on (`~`), every element (`:nth-*`); `incr_style` calls it once per changed parent after the per-entry marks (also in the check-mode reconcile). (2) Seed 2475, hidden behind (1): removing an element whose node is freed at once (no handle to walk) removed only its own entry; its descendants' entries stayed, with child lists naming freed text nodes, whose addresses a new text node can reuse, so `text_parent` found the stale parent and a later text edit was lost (a kept box kept the old text). `drop_key` drops the descendants through the stored lists, and `text_parent` only accepts a live parent that still holds the text node. Tests: `qinc1f_fix_*` in incr_style_tests.rs, `child_list_marks_old_and_new_edges_and_changed_siblings` in invalidation_tests.rs. The fuzz test runs 1 000 cases in release (CI) and 200 in debug, plus the seven seeds (`REGRESSION_SEEDS`).

## QINC1k4: pseudo-element viewport-height reads (R60 "QINC1k4 DONE"; agent item)

> QINC1k4 (P2, assigned engine correctness fix; blocks flipping the SCRATCHY_INCR default). From QINC1k2 #466: in 1 of 3 window check-mode runs on github.com 20 style mismatches appeared: `slot after/before field width ... Calc(..,(956.0,312.0)) vs (956.0,485.0)` on footer links and a carousel indicator. Find which vh the slot captured and why the engine didn't recompute it; build a deterministic repro (a viewport-height change between frames with a ::before/::after using vh in calc, with and without a restart/adoption in between), fix it in the engine, and verify. Tests: the repro test; fuzz 0 mismatches (7 windows; add viewport-height changes to the fuzz step set if absent). Gate: `gate.sh check 3 github` and `gate.sh check 1` on the other pages: no slot mismatches.

**What changed:** cause: the engine's element visit kept only the ELEMENT slot's viewport-height read flag (`Entry::reads_vh`) and dropped the pseudo slots' (`style_of(..).0`), so an element whose `::before` / `::after` / `::marker` read the viewport height (a `vh` unit, or any `%`-bearing `calc()`, which captures the whole `(vw, vh)` pair in `BoxLength::Calc`) was not re-cascaded on a height-only change and its pseudo kept the old pair (github: the window height went 312 -> 485 between two engine updates). Not adoption-specific: an adopted record and an incremental cascade lost it the same way. `incr_style.rs`: an element's `reads_vh` is the OR of its own and its pseudo slots' reads. `incr_fuzz_tests.rs`: viewport-height steps (`HEIGHTS`) and `vh` / `%`-calc rules on elements and pseudo slots (a second sheet), drawn from a second per-seed generator so the existing page / mutation streams and `REGRESSION_SEEDS` are unchanged (without the fix the debug window fails on 8+ seeds). Test: `qinc1k4_pseudo_calc_viewport_height_change_recascades`. Numbers in R60.

## QINC1k1: translation invariance in y for content heights (R60 "QINC1k1 DONE"; agent item)

> QINC1k1 (P1, blocks flipping SCRATCHY_INCR default; assigned correctness fix under the QINC1 freeze). github.com window runs with SCRATCHY_INCR=1 SCRATCHY_INCR_CHECK=1 report 13-14 `style.height: Some(Px(642.0005)) vs Some(Px(642.0))` mismatches on a `position:absolute; inset:0; height:100%` element: its positioned parent's auto height is `cursor_y - content_y` in document coordinates, so it depends on where the box sits; the engine shifts the clean subtree and keeps the old value. Repro tools/incr-gate/abs-drift.html. Choose the fix that makes the engine exact without hiding real differences: preferred, sum content heights relative to content_y if from-scratch output differs only in sub-ulp rounding (WPT, full suite, screenshots unchanged); alternatively guard engine-side (measure the hit-rate cost); not just a tolerance. **What changed:** `layout.rs`: the auto content height is summed relative to the content box (`ry` beside `cursor_y`, which still places the children) in the block arm, `measure_table`, `measure_grid` and `measure_flex` (row / column report their items' relative bottom edge). Floats stay in document space, so a BFC root holding floats and a flow position taken from a float mark the box `Ck::y_sensitive` (`layout::Y_SENS`, inherited through cache hits); `incr_layout::try_hit` reuses such a box only at the same y (`incr.miss_y`). `paint.rs` `fill_rect` counts an edge within 1e-3 px below a pixel boundary as on it (with the exact relative heights bbc.com's `bottom: 0` banner ended at 484.99957 and lost its last row). Q48d clearance resolves a `%` / `calc()` margin-top instead of `px()` (fuzz find). Tests: `qinc1k1_*` in incr_layout_tests.rs (block, flex row / column / wrap, grid, table; a float BFC root), `qinc1k1_fill_rect_edges_within_rounding_noise_snap_to_the_pixel_boundary`, `qinc1k1_clearance_resolves_a_percentage_margin_top` and `qinc1k1_fuzz_fractional_heights_far_down` (main code: 378 of 1 000 cases fail; now 0 of 7 000). github check gate 0 mismatches in 6 runs, other pages 0 in 12, `miss_y` 0 on all pages, WPT unchanged. From QINC1k1 #468 (R60 "QINC1k1 DONE" in scratchy/REGRESSIONS.md): the incremental-engine fuzz harness found an 8 px `style.width` mismatch (engine vs from-scratch: 504 vs 512 — a percentage resolved against 1008 vs 1024) after a mutation moving `li.c1.c4` under a parent matched by `div .c1{width:50%}`. It also happens on main. The full page and steps are in scratchy/tools/incr-gate/fuzz-width-504-512.txt; a hand-written minimal test did not reproduce it. Reproduce it from that file (replay through the fuzz harness machinery in src/tests/incr_fuzz_tests.rs), minimise, find the cause, fix it in the engine, add a regression seed/test. Another agent works QINC1k3 in src/incr_layout.rs in parallel — if the fix must go in incr_layout.rs, keep it minimal and say so. Tests: the replay as a regression test; fuzz harness 7 windows 0 mismatches (incl. qinc1k1_fuzz_fractional_heights_far_down); full suite; `scratchy/tools/incr-gate/gate.sh check 1` on all pages 0 mismatches.

**What changed:** the mismatching box is the li's absolute `::before` (`width:50%`), whose containing block moved from the viewport (1024) to `div.c0` (1008). The bottom-up walk's failed attempts put fresh copies of its z entry into the harvest; two cancelled out (a key with two `Laid`s serves neither), and the old tree's copy put afterwards was then served alone to the `<html>` hit. `incr_layout.rs` (small change, QINC1k3 works there too): `AMBIGUOUS`, per update, so a key that ever held two `Laid`s serves no later copy. Tests: `qinc1k10_replay_fuzz_width_504_512` (replays the recorded page; fails on main), `qinc1k10_harvest_key_with_two_laids_stays_unserved`, `qinc1k10_moved_abs_pseudo_resolves_against_its_new_containing_block`. Fuzz 7 + 7 windows 0 mismatches, suite 1 736, clippy 77, WPT unchanged; `gate.sh check 1` all 7 pages 0 mismatches (R60).

Find why the bottom-up walk in src/incr_layout.rs doesn't stop below the root on Wikipedia (layout_up_reasons / layout_root_reasons counters) and fix the dominant reasons, keeping exactness. Also check the ~9.3 ms restyle per frame (what is restyled on a hover/scroll frame on Wikipedia, and whether invalidation is too broad). Recipe: scratchy/tools/incr-gate/gate.sh perf 3 wiki. Gate: Wikipedia INCR=1 App builds <= 20 % of flag off (or explain the floor), root walks substantially down; other pages (ytr ytw github bbc hover) not worse than R60 QINC1k/QINC1k2 numbers; `gate.sh check 1` on all pages 0 mismatches; fuzz harness incl. qinc1k1_fuzz_fractional_heights_far_down 0 mismatches.

**What changed:** a temporary per-frame trace (removed) showed (a) the ~10 ms restyle frames were ~95 % the document-wide counter / quote walk (`generated`, ~10 ms on Wikipedia's ~9 300 elements), re-run on every DOM write; (b) every walk to the root went up through `not_cacheable` boxes: Wikipedia's article floats (thumbnails, infobox) live in the root BFC, so every box after the first float (`floats_in`) and every ancestor of one (`floats_out`) was uncacheable, and both the hovered paragraph's walk and a popup appended to `<body>` re-measured most of the page. `incr_style.rs`: each entry keeps `gsig`, a hash of what the walk reads of it (display none, quotes, own content, counter properties, `::before` / `::after` content parts, ol/ul/li; `GEN_ATTR` when a content reads `attr()`); the walk runs only when an entry's `gsig` changes, a non-zero one is inserted / moved / removed, an attribute of a `GEN_ATTR` element changes, or a write lands where the engine keeps no entries (under `display: none`). `layout.rs` / `incr_layout.rs`: `Ck::fl` records the floats a box was measured among (shared `Arc` snapshot) and the floats its measure placed; such a box is reused only at the same origin among bit-identical floats (and re-places its floats), and the bottom-up attempt re-measures it among the same floats and splices only when it placed the same floats (`floats_out_changed`); a BFC root among floats still goes up (`bfc_among_floats`: its parent places it by its min-content width). `tools/incr-gate/run.sh`: `INJECT_W` / `INJECT_H` (absolute inject coordinates on a short nested tile). Tests: 3 style (`qinc1k3_counter_walk_*`) + 3 layout (`qinc1k3_*`) + 2 updated QINC1h1/QINC1j-ab tests. Measured (window, 960x1006, 3 interleaved pairs vs main e5f64e4): Wikipedia INCR=1 App builds 13-14 % of flag off (main 38 %), root walks 133-134 -> 60, relayout 1.44 s -> 0.23 s, restyle 1.96 s -> 0.89 s per run; other pages not worse. Exactness: `gate.sh check 1` 7 pages 0 mismatches, fuzz 0..9000 x 1 000 0 mismatches, suite 1 742, clippy 77, WPT unchanged (R60).

## QWPT1: conformance plan (R64; Opus investigator, design only)

> QWPT1 [M, Opus, design only] (P1, user 2026-11-21 architecture discussion) Conformance plan, as a design memo in REGRESSIONS.md for the user to approve BEFORE any implementation: (a) run WPT testharness.js tests: today the runner (src/wpt.rs skip_reason) skips every testharness test and the local checkout (/home/loupax/src/wpt) has only css/ and html/. Plan the checkout (sparse dirs: dom/, html/webappapis, html/semantics, css/cssom, css/cssom-view, fetch/, resize-observer/, intersection-observer/, uievents/, ...), the harness (testharnessreport hook, timeouts, per-subtest results), expectations file and CI cost. (b) a per-spec-area pass-rate report tracked like wpt-expected.txt, and the dependency order of areas (DOM core -> events -> HTML event loop / rendering steps -> CSSOM -> geometry -> fetch/streams -> media). (c) an audit of the event loop against HTML "update the rendering" (task/microtask/rAF/observer order). (d) a missing-API report for real sites: log calls to unimplemented APIs and failed feature probes. (e) offline recorded pages so the incr-gate perf runs are deterministic and can become CI budgets. Size every follow-up item; the user decides the order.

**What changed:** docs only (REGRESSIONS.md R64, this entry); no product code. Counts come from WPT's published manifest for the pin (33,150 testharness files, 29,177 reftests) and `git ls-tree`. A throwaway probe inlined 1,522 self-contained testharness tests (dom, html/webappapis, css/cssom, css/cssom-view, the observers, uievents, url, encoding, webidl, hr-time, streams) and ran them through `scratchy --js-report --run-timers`: 98 % reported, 10,253 of 23,389 subtests pass (44 %), mean per-file score 31 %, 39 s wall at 4 jobs; process start ~59 ms per test; the reftest runner takes 0.9 s. Plan: a static mount in wire (scratchy stays socket-free; wptserve later for `.py` handlers), a `--wpt-th` runner (one process per test, virtual clock, 30 s wall cap), per-area expectation files and a committed `wpt-th/areas.txt` score table (wpt.fyi-style per-file score). Event-loop audit: 15 deviations (E1-E15) with function names, the main ones rAF as a 60 Hz timer, ResizeObserver 0x0 and never re-delivered, IntersectionObserver evaluated at timer boundaries, no scroll events for user scrolling, timer/rAF exceptions not reported to `onerror`, setInterval always clamped to 4 ms, scripts run after the full parse. Missing-API report: one forwarding Proxy at the end of the window/DOM prototype chains in report mode only. Recording: `wire --record/--replay` plus `--deterministic`; first budgets listed. 26 follow-up items (QWPT2-9, QEL1-9, QMAPI1-3, QREC1-3, QBUD1, QAREA-DOM) and 8 user questions (R64 section 7). Recommended first: QWPT2, QWPT3, QWPT4a.

> QFLK5 [S] (P2, from #460 CI; Sonnet) V8 heap-growth tests qpt1b_fifty_create_remove_cycles_return_to_baseline (main CI e219bee) and qpt1e_nosnap_create_remove_cycles (#460) flake on CI. CI e219bee measured a residual heap delta of 2 418 856 bytes over 50 cycles against a 1 MiB limit (all realms were gone, 0 0). `__scratchy_heap_gc` (test seam in `js_engine_v8.rs`) now repeats `low_memory_notification` until the used size stops falling (max 6 passes); the test warms up with 10 cycles plus a collection (was 3) and the limit is 8 MiB. ## QFLK6: window images keyed by the document, not its node address (agent item)

> QFLK6 [S] (P3, from #463; Sonnet) qinc1i_forced_layouts_see_the_windows_images flakes: window images keyed by a document's node address, which a new document can reuse. Key by a document id.

**What changed:** `incr_engine.rs` `WINDOW_IMAGES` held `node_id(doc)` (the document node's address); once the old document was dropped a new one could be allocated at the same address and inherit its images. The slot now holds a `WeakHandle` to the document and `is_doc` compares by `Rc::ptr_eq` after `upgrade()`. The weak handle keeps the allocation alive, so no new node can reuse the address, and a dead or different document never matches (an identity without a counter: the parser creates documents and has no hook to stamp an id). Test: `qflk6_a_new_document_never_sees_a_dropped_documents_images` (incr_forced_tests.rs; drops a document that had images, then creates documents: fails on main with "address reused: true", passes now). `qinc1i_forced_layouts_see_the_windows_images` 20 runs in a row green, full suite 1 744 passed. Not changed: `incr_box` / `incr_layout` `doc_key` still use `node_id` (they also compare `base_ver`).

## QFLK4: q30d typing test flake = shared system clipboard (agent item)

> QFLK4 [S] (P3, from QNAV9 #435; Sonnet) forms test q30d_typing_through_the_app_events_maxlength_readonly_escape failed once in a full suite run while the machine was loaded (passed in 2 later runs). Find the timing dependence; prove 20x.

**What changed:** the timing dependence is which test thread wins the process's single winit `EventLoop` (every `q30d_*` App test does `EventLoop::build()` and silently `return`s on Err). Alone, the test deterministically FAILS: `js_dom` `__scratchy_dn` built `beforeinput`/`input` as plain `Event`, so pages saw no `inputType`/`data` (expected `insertText`/`a`). In a full run it usually lost the loop race and passed vacuously; when it won (load changes thread scheduling) it failed. Fix: `__scratchy_dn` now uses `InputEvent` for `beforeinput` and `input` (real product bug). Also hardened a second race: under `cfg!(test)` `forms_text::clipboard_set/get` use only the internal clipboard, so the Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V step cannot read text another process put on the desktop clipboard. Proof: before, 10/40 failures at load 20-55; after, 20/20 alone, 20/20 with the q30d_ group, full suite 1743 pass, load 27-60.

## QJ4b: grid implicit tracks (no out-of-range panic in measure_grid)

> QJ4b [S] (P3, found by QJ4) Layout PANIC in measure_grid (col_widths[col_start..col_end] out of range) on theguardian.com/international. Fix the grid algorithm per CSS Grid, not the site.

**What changed:** the column count is now derived from the items (named area width, definite line ends, spans), not just the explicit track list. Extra columns are implicit tracks sized by the new `grid-auto-columns` (default `auto`, cycled); the new `grid-auto-rows` sizes implicit rows. Auto-placement wraps at the explicit width (or the widest span), line numbers are capped at 1000 (spec limit) so `grid-column: 1 / 99999999` cannot allocate, and `free()` slices are bounds-checked. Root cause: a named area (or line placement) starting at/after the last track gave col_end = col_start+1 > track count. Tests: qj4b_* in src/tests/flex_grid_tests.rs.

## QSTASH1: src/stash.rs, the localStorage state directory (STASH.md; agent item)

> QSTASH1 [M] (P2) `src/stash.rs`: the state directory and its rules, no JS wiring. Layout, key<->filename encoding (percent-encode `/`, `%`, NUL, a leading `.`, a trailing `~`; empty key `%`; >200 bytes -> `%h<sha256>` with the key on the first line), WTF-8 values with the one-`\n` rule, `load(site, origin) -> sorted pairs`, `commit(site, origin, generation, ops)` on a writer thread, `clear`, `forget(site)`, the per-site flock and generation number exactly as STASH.md "Locking", the 5 MB per-origin check under the lock, and the unusable-directory fallback (one log line). Tests (new `src/tests/stash_tests.rs`, temp directories): encoding round-trips incl. lone surrogates and every escaped case; a file written by hand without/with a final newline; dotfiles and `*~` ignored; two `File` handles contend on the lock (flock is per open file description, so this works inside one test process); a commit after forget with a stale generation is dropped; forget while a commit waits does not resurrect.

**What changed:** new `src/stash.rs` (no callers yet; QSTASH2 wires it): `Stash::open` (mode 0700, `storage/.locks/`, a write probe) / `open_or_log` (the STASH.md fallback line, once per process), `load` (shared flock; generation + pairs sorted by key), `commit` (exclusive flock; a generation other than the lock file's -> `Forgotten`, nothing written; `.tmp-<pid>-<n>` + fsync + rename, unlink, directory fsync; usage recounted from the files under the lock, a set that takes the origin over 5 Mi UTF-16 code units of keys plus values is skipped with a log line), `clear`, `forget` (`rm -r storage/<site>`, generation +1 written in place in the lock file so its inode stays), `Writer` (thread, in-order commits, `flush`, joins on drop). Keys and values are `Vec<u16>`, WTF-8 on disk (in-tree encoder/decoder; a non-WTF-8 hand-made file is skipped, never decoded lossily). `site_dir_name` / `origin_dir_name` (opaque origins -> None). Locks use std `File::lock` / `lock_shared` (stable since Rust 1.89; CI pins 1.96.1); the SHA-256 for long key names is a small in-tree function like `ws_frames::sha1`: no new crate. Tests: `qstash1_*` in `src/tests/stash_tests.rs`, in directories under `target/stash-tests/`.

## QSTASH2: localStorage over stash (agent item)

> QSTASH2 [M] (P2, after QSTASH1) localStorage over stash. `--state-dir` flag (+ `SCRATCHY_STATE_DIR`). At page start (`startup_engine`/`run_page`, before the first script) load the origin's pairs into the prelude's Storage Map; opaque origins (file:, data:, about:) keep today's in-memory Storage. setItem/removeItem/clear record ops; the App hands them to the stash writer thread at the end of each task; QuotaExceededError over 5 MB. Keys and values cross from V8 as UTF-16 code units, encoded to WTF-8 by stash: never `to_rust_string_lossy` or another UTF-8 conversion, which turns lone surrogates into U+FFFD. Tests: a value set on one page is there on the next page load and after a new App with the same --state-dir; file: pages do not persist; quota throws; ops from one task land together; a value with a lone surrogate (`"a\uD83D"`) reads back identical after a reload. Real check: social.loupax.com `:set novim` survives a restart (user's vim.js case, which stores `localStorage.vimOff`).

**What changed:** new `src/js_storage.rs`. `--state-dir DIR` / `SCRATCHY_STATE_DIR` / `$XDG_STATE_HOME/scratchy` / `~/.local/state/scratchy` opens a thread-local `Backend` (a `Stash` and its `Writer` thread) in window mode (not with `--no-js`); `--js-report` only with an explicit `--state-dir`; `--wpt`, `--perf-report` and tests never, so headless runs never write the user's storage. `startup_engine` evaluates `__scratchy_ls_fill()` after the env, before the first page script: for an http(s) page it flushes the writer (the previous page's engine is dropped after the next one starts, so its last commit must land first), loads the origin under the top-level site and fills the prelude's `Map`; opaque origins get `undefined` and stay in memory. The prelude's Storage is now an "area" (`Map` + a running count of UTF-16 code units); `setItem` checks `stash::QUOTA_UNITS` (5 Mi code units of keys plus values) in JS and throws `QuotaExceededError` (code 22) before anything is recorded, then calls `__scratchy_ls_op`; setting the same value, removing a missing key and clearing an empty store record nothing. `JsEngine::storage_end_task` (end of `eval_as` and `drain_after_task`, i.e. every task) hands that task's ops to the writer as one commit; the engine's `LocalStorage` field hands the rest over when the page goes away, and `run()` drops the App and flushes the writer before exit. A commit that reports `Forgotten` empties the page's copy. Strings cross as UTF-16 through the new `js_engine::Utf16` (`write_v2` / `new_from_two_byte`), never a UTF-8 conversion. Same-origin iframe realms share the parent's localStorage and sessionStorage areas (`__scratchy_ls_share` in `__scratchy_realm_init`); opaque (data:) frames keep their own. `:help`, NOTES.md and STASH.md document the flag. Tests: `qstash2_*` in `src/tests/stash_tests.rs` (next page load and a restart on the same dir, a second App via `handle_nav_result`, file:/about:/data: and no-backend pages do not persist, the exact quota boundary in memory and on disk, one task's three ops = one commit, `"a\uD83D"` and a lone-surrogate key round-trip with WTF-8 bytes on disk, a srcdoc iframe shares the page's storage, state-dir resolution, an unusable dir stays in memory).

## QSTASH5: wire --cookie-file and X-Wire-Cookie-Op: clear-site (W-PERSIST1; agent item)

> QSTASH5 [S] (P2, wire) `wire --cookie-file PATH` and `X-Wire-Cookie-Op: clear-site`. See wire/TODO.txt W-PERSIST1.

**What changed:** wire only (`wire/src/cookies.rs`, `wire/src/main.rs`). `--cookie-file PATH`: the jar loads at start (expired cookies dropped; a missing file is a fresh jar; a corrupt or unreadable one is one log line and an empty jar, replaced at the next save) and a saver thread writes it at most once a second while it has changes, and once more on SIGTERM (handler only sets an atomic flag), via temp file + fsync + rename + directory fsync, mode 0600. Tests: `every_cookie_control_op_needs_the_token`, `page_requests_through_the_jar_do_not_need_the_token`, `token_file_is_mode_0600_next_to_the_socket_and_replaced_on_every_start` (wire); `qstash5_*` in `src/tests/net_policy_tests.rs` (scratchy). > QSTASH3 [S] `scratchy --forget-site <site or URL>`: stash forget (lock, `rm -r`, generation bump) plus wire `X-Wire-Cookie-Op: clear-site` (with the control token, re-read on a 403); if wire is unreachable the stash part still runs and the log says the cookies were not cleared. **What changed:** new `src/forget.rs`, dispatched from `run()` when `--forget-site` appears (headless, no window). The argument is a URL or a bare host (`https://` assumed); hosts with empty labels (`..`) are refused so the directory name is always one plain component. `Stash::forget(site)` removes exactly `storage/<site>` and bumps the generation; then `clear-site` goes to wire (`control_token(socket, false)` + `cookie_control_headers`, one retry after a 403 with a re-read token). ## QREC2: --deterministic (agent item)

> QREC2 [S] scratchy --deterministic (report modes): V8 --random-seed, seeded crypto.getRandomValues, Date epoch from the recording, network results delivered in request order.

**What changed:** `--deterministic[=EPOCH_MS]` (js.rs `take_deterministic_flag`, called first in `run()`; accepted only with `--perf-report`, `--js-report`, `--missing-api-report` or `--wpt-th-one` as first argument, else exit 2). Effects: V8 `--random-seed` set in `init_v8` before the platform/isolate exist (covers Math.random); `os_random_bytes` (getRandomValues, randomUUID) becomes a seeded splitmix64 stream; a Date shim after the preludes starts at the epoch and advances 1 ms per read, independent of the wall clock. Epoch: scratchy does not read the recording; the caller passes it (recording `t_ms` is relative, so use the recording's date, e.g. `$(stat -c %Y DIR/index.jsonl)000`); a bare flag uses 1700000000000. Network: the report drivers (`drive_report_net`) already run requests one at a time in queue order, so results arrive in request order; only the window's per-request threads race, and window mode is never deterministic. Test: `tests/deterministic.rs` (binary against a fake wire socket that answers the first fetch late): two deterministic runs identical, two plain runs differ. Documented in `:help`. Not covered: performance.now() and timers still use the real clock.

## QDOM4: Event flags per DOM (agent item)

> QDOM4 [S] (P1; Sonnet; js.rs Event + ETP.dispatchEvent; R65) Event flags per DOM 2.x: stop propagation, stop immediate, canceled, initialized, dispatch; cancelBubble, returnValue, initEvent during dispatch, composedPath after dispatch, listener exceptions reported and dispatch continues, handleEvent looked up at every invoke, isTrusted own unforgeable getter, srcElement, passive-by-default for touchstart/touchmove/wheel/mousewheel on window/document/html/body.

**What changed:** js.rs: flags are hidden slots (cleared at the end of dispatch, cancelBubble set before dispatch stops it, a stop at the target's capture invoke skips its bubble invoke); `isTrusted` is one shared own non-configurable getter backed by a WeakSet (`__scratchy_trust`, used by the UA event path in js_dom.rs); `returnValue`, `srcElement`; `initEvent` is a no-op while dispatching and resets stop/canceled/target; dispatching an event that is being dispatched or an uninitialized `createEvent` event throws InvalidStateError; listener and `on<type>` exceptions go through `__scratchy_report_error` (QERR1) and dispatch continues; `handleEvent` is read per invoke (a non-callable one is a reported TypeError); passive defaults; a minimal `window.event` (QDOM10 refines it); inline handlers are not compiled in documents without a browsing context. WPT: dom/events 23.0 -> 32.5. Reported listener exceptions turn 22 files that swallowed them from OK to ERROR (no subtest pass lost); recorded.

## QDOM1: window named access (agent item)

> QDOM1 [S] (P1; Sonnet; js.rs, js_dom.rs; R65) Window named access and indexed child windows: a WindowProperties object between Window.prototype and EventTarget.prototype; get/has by element id or embed/form/img/object name (native `__d_named`, cached by `wgen`), iframe name -> contentWindow, `window[i]`.

**What changed:** js.rs: `WindowProperties` is a Proxy (get/has only; its target inherits EventTarget.prototype) set as the prototype of `Window.prototype`; names found anywhere else in the chain are not shadowed, own globals and `var`s win, nothing is enumerable. js_dom.rs: native `__d_named(doc, name)` builds one name -> element map per DOM write generation; the DOM prelude hands the proxy a resolver (index -> `winAt`, iframe -> its window, else the element wrapper). Known deviation: with a Proxy in the global's chain V8 does not throw ReferenceError for a strict-mode assignment to an undeclared name (reads still do); the qj1/qy15 tests probe strictness with `NaN = 1` instead. Tests: qdom1_window_named_access.

## QEL1: rendering-steps driver (agent item)

> QEL1 [M] (P1; new src/event_loop.rs, app.rs, js.rs TIMERS_PRELUDE; R64 section 4 E1-E3; after QWPT4b so the change is measured) Rendering-steps driver shared by the App and the headless runner: one function runs, per frame: resize -> scroll events -> MQL change -> animation events -> rAF batch (own id space, one timestamp, never split by the timer slice) -> style/layout through the engine -> [RO, IO hooks] -> paint (App only). TIMERS_PRELUDE: rAF has its own list and per-realm id space (iframe realms forward to the parent's list), `__scratchy_raf_due/begin/run_one`; `JsEngine::run_animation_frames` runs the whole batch with one timestamp, one eval (budget + microtask checkpoint) per callback; rAF exceptions are reported at the callback's own global. ## QCSS1: stylesheet `@media` uses the matchMedia evaluator (agent item)

> QCSS1 [S] (P1, from QMAPI2 #523; css.rs @media parser) The stylesheet `@media` parser only knew min-width, max-width, prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion; range syntax, hover/pointer, orientation, resolution... dropped the whole rule while `matchMedia` already understood them. One implementation.

**What changed:** css.rs: `MediaQuery` is now one comma-list item's text plus a memo (viewport w/h + reduced-motion -> answer) evaluated by `media_one_query_eval`, the same code `matchMedia` runs (`media_query_string_matches`); `parse_media_query_list` just splits the prelude at top-level commas. `not`, `or`, nested conditions, range syntax, hover/pointer, orientation, aspect-ratio, resolution now work in `@media`. Height-reading queries note a viewport-height read; incr_style.rs forces a full re-match when the height changes and some rule's media reads it (matches are cached per element, a height-only resize otherwise left stale matches: caught by the shadow check). Side effect: `@media not print` now applies on screen, so WPT reftest css/printing/transition-in-media-print.tentative.html (which passed only because `not` was treated as never-matching) now fails, as every browser's screen rendering would. Tests: cascade_tests `qcss1_*` (each syntax form, stylesheet vs matchMedia agreement, height-only resize). `<link media>` / `<style media>` / `@import ... media` are not parsed anywhere yet (separate item).

## QDOM12: Text.splitText, Text.wholeText, Node.normalize (agent item)

> QDOM12 [S] (P2) `Text.splitText(offset)` (IndexSizeError, new node after it, live range updates once QDOM5 has them), `Text.wholeText`, `Node.normalize()` (merge adjacent Text, drop empty, on Document and Element).

**What changed:** js_dom.rs (next to the CharacterData methods): `Text.prototype.splitText` (clones the node so a CDATASection splits into a CDATASection; offset converted as unsigned long), `Text.prototype.wholeText` (contiguous Text/CDATA siblings), `Node.prototype.normalize` (exclusive Text only; empty nodes removed, runs merged with one `__d_settext` then the rest removed). All steps use the logging natives, so MutationObserver records and incremental-engine change notes come for free. `rangeHook.split/merge` are the (no-op) places for the live-Range fix-ups of the spec; QDOM3 (#533) was not on main yet, so ranges do not follow splits/merges yet. Tests: qdom12_tests.rs (also run engine-forced via qdom12_incr_forced_tests.rs).

> QDOM3 [S] (P1, R65; js_dom.rs) `ParentNode.moveBefore(node, child)` on Element, Document and DocumentFragment: a state-preserving move, WPT dom/nodes/moveBefore/*.

**What changed:** js_dom.rs: pre-move checks (same shadow-including root, which also covers connected-ness and cross-document; not a host-including inclusive ancestor of the parent; Element or CharacterData only; no Element/Text directly in a Document; NotFoundError for a `child` of another parent; TypeError for a non-Node or a missing second argument), then the native `__d_move`, which shares `insert_native` with `__d_insert` (same tree edit and incr_log ChildRemove/ChildInsert, so layout sees the move) but skips the `<link>` rescan and every JS-side insertion hook (script prepare, iframe load, ownership bookkeeping), so scripts do not re-run, iframes keep their document, focus stays. The JS side keeps what the spec keeps: NodeIterator pre-remove steps, live Range fix-ups (new `live` WeakRef list in the Range block; removal fix at the old place, insertion fix at the new one), one removal + one insertion MutationObserver record, and per custom element `connectedMoveCallback` (else disconnectedCallback + connectedCallback, element by element in tree order). Tests: js_dom_tests `qdom3_*`, js_geometry_tests `qdom3_move_before_updates_layout` (also runs engine-forced). WPT dom/nodes score 48.5 -> 55.1. `css-transition-trigger.html` now TIMEOUTs (30 s) instead of failing at once: it waits for `transitionstart`, which needs CSS transitions on a moved subtree (recorded in wpt-th/expected). Not done: ElementInternals, CSS transitions/animations continuing across a move, focus events. Ranges are still only live for `moveBefore` (insert/remove fix-ups stay QDOM5).

## QWPTFLK3: parser-sets-attributes-after-built-in-constructor regression on #543 CI (agent item)

> QWPTFLK3 (investigation + fix) custom-elements/parser/parser-sets-attributes-after-built-in-constructor.html: subtest "Live getElementsByClassName reflects a empty class attribute appended by the parser after the constructor inserted the element" regressed 5/5 on release-build CI for PR #543 (passes locally, other PRs green); decide real bug or flakiness, fix with a test or keep in flaky.txt with the mechanism.

**Found:** a real bug, not flakiness. The test's constructors do `container.append(this)` during the upgrade that `customElements.define` starts; the insert hook scanned the inserted element, saw no `ceState` yet and upgraded it AGAIN from inside its own constructor, recursing until V8 threw "Maximum call stack size exceeded" (one run logged 3 + 44 RangeErrors and 1877 follow-on TypeErrors). Which frame got the RangeError depends on the stack frame sizes of the binary, so the outcome was deterministic per build (5/5 on #543's binary, 0/30 single and 0/30 area runs locally, quiet and at load 17-37) and independent of load: a scratch probe that calls `define` at stack depths 0..1480 (step 37) failed at 7 of 41 depths with the unfixed release binary (period ~185 frames), at 0 of 41 with the fix. Two stale-cache paths turned the overflow into wrong collection contents: `cids` recorded the DOM generation before running the producer, and `safeQ` turned the RangeError into "no match", so the live collection cached `[]` for that generation. **What changed (js_dom.rs):** `ceUpgrade` returns when the element already has a state and marks it failed (-1) while the constructor runs (DOM upgrade steps 1 and 4); `cids` sets `s.wg` only after the producer returned; `safeQ` rethrows RangeError. Tests: src/tests/qwptflk3_tests.rs (3). Removed from wpt-th/flaky.txt (added by #543); areas.txt regenerated with `--areas-only`. Full --wpt-th: no regressions; custom-element-reaction-queue.html 0/6 -> 1/6, upgrading.html 22/28 -> 24/28 (re-recorded).

## QDOM13: event handler IDL attributes (agent item)

> QDOM13 [S] (P2; js.rs attrHandler/`fwd`, js_dom.rs; R65) Event handler IDL attributes as accessors: GlobalEventHandlers/WindowEventHandlers/DocumentAndElementEventHandlers on HTMLElement, Document and Window (default null; setting a non-function stores null; the content attribute still compiles lazily). `<body>`/`<frameset>` onload/onerror/onresize/... get/set the Window's handler. onanimation*/ontransition* and the legacy webkitAnimation*/webkitTransitionEnd mapping. No ontouch* on window/document. HTMLFrameSetElement. WPT: dom/events/webkit-*-event, Body-FrameSet-Event-Handlers.

**What changed:** js.rs: `attrHandler` replaced by per-(target, type) handler slots (`getH`/`setH`). A non-null IDL value registers ONE entry in the target's listener list (a handler runs in registration order among the listeners; `removeEventListener(type, null)` cannot hit it). A never-overridden content attribute still compiles lazily and runs after the listeners. A changed or re-set content attribute wins over an earlier IDL value (`__scratchy_attr_changed`, called from `setAttribute`/`removeAttribute`); the attribute is read in the null namespace (`__d_getns`), so `setAttributeNS(ns, 'onclick', ...)` does not count. Accessors (enumerable, configurable, on the prototypes Chrome uses) for ~100 names on HTMLElement/SVGElement/Document/Window; `onwebkitanimation*`/`onwebkittransitionend` with their prefixed event types; Window-only names on Window and on `<body>`/`<frameset>`, where `onblur/onerror/onfocus/onload/onresize/onscroll` and the Window-only names forward to the Window (the content attribute of ANY body/frameset of the document too). DOM "inner invoke" step 8: a trusted animationstart/iteration/end/transitionend with no unprefixed listener or handler on that node fires the prefixed ones, with `event.type` set to the prefixed name. `HTMLFrameSetElement` interface. Left out on purpose: `ontouch*` (touch-device sniffing) and `onscrollend/onscrollsnapchange/onscrollsnapchanging` (scratchy never fires them, and tests feature-detect `window.onscrollend` to wait for one: css/cssom-view/scrollIntoView-multiple* regressed while they existed).

## QANIMHL: CSS animation events in the headless rendering steps (agent item)

> QANIMHL [S] (P2, from QDOM13 #557) CSS animation/transition events never fire in the headless test child (`--wpt-th-one`): a @keyframes rule (insertRule or <style> text) plus `animation: 1ms` fires no animationstart/end; the 4 dom/events/webkit-*-event files now TIMEOUT waiting for them. Find whether it is the runner's rendering step (QEL1 headless frames), the engine's style/animation timeline, or event delivery; fix; list every --wpt-th file that changes.

**Found:** two causes, neither in event delivery. (1) The headless rendering host had no animation step at all: `Headless` used the trait defaults (no `update_animations`), the document clock stayed 0 and nothing fed an `AnimTracker` (only the App's builds do), so headless frames never advanced or reported an animation. (2) An empty `@keyframes anim {}` (what the webkit-* tests insert) was skipped by `anim_eval::evaluate` and `is_animated` in EVERY mode, so it fired no events in the App window either (nested window: main fires a 500 ms animation's start/end but nothing for the empty one; this branch fires both). Transitions are not implemented in the engine at all (webkit-transition-end-event and the transitionend subtests stay TIMEOUT).

**What changed:** event_loop.rs `Headless { js, now }` + `HeadlessAnim` (in `JsEngine`): step 6 runs the page's forced layout (`__d_anim_pass` -> `GeomCache::style_pass`) at the page clock when the page has `@keyframes` and its DOM changed; the pass's report (`anim_eval::animation_passes`) goes to the tracker; step 4 of the next update ticks it and dispatches the events before rAF; `headless_frame_due` adds the animation due time. Empty keyframes run (events, no value change). getComputedStyle's cache keys animated entries on the clock. The pass counts as `io` (rendering update) in --perf-report. Tests: src/tests/qanimhl_tests.rs (8). Gates: full --wpt-th: dom/nodes moveBefore continue-css-animation-left/-transform 0/1 -> 1/1, css-animation-commit-styles subtest TIMEOUT -> FAIL, dom/events EventListener-invoke-legacy 0/6 -> 2/6; with QDOM13 #557 merged locally the three webkit-animation-{start,end,iteration}-event files go 4/13 -> 13/13. Reftest subset unchanged (340/286). --perf-report (own wire, recorded then replayed): GitHub +1 rendering-step layout (~480 ms, `io`), YouTube results script-forced layouts 17 -> 9 (the step lays out first), totals within noise.

## QANIMHLb: CSS transitions (agent item)

> QANIMHLb [M] (P2, from QANIMHL #562) CSS transitions: the engine has none (no `transition`/`transition-*` parsing, no interpolation on style change, no transitionrun/start/end/cancel). Implement per CSS Transitions 1 for the properties the animation engine can already interpolate (start on computed-value change, delay/duration/timing-function, cancel on removal/display:none, events in the rendering step before rAF, both App and headless). Gates: dom/events/webkit-transition-end-event.html, EventListener-invoke-legacy transitionend subtests, css areas in --wpt-th, reftests, --perf-report on gate pages, live window check (a hover transition).

**What changed:** new src/transition.rs: `transition` + `transition-property/duration/timing-function/delay/behavior` (and `-webkit-`/`-moz-` aliases) parse into `Declarations::trans`, cascade into an interned `TransRef` (`ComputedStyle::transitions`). Engine: `transition::apply` at the end of `resolve_style_for` keeps each transitioning element's last base style (a compact snapshot of the transitionable fields) and starts / replaces / reverses (§3.1 shortening) transitions when a base value changes; idempotent across repeated resolves; read-only in the incremental shadow run; `display:none`, removal (pass / membership ageing) and an unlisted property cancel. Properties: the `lerp_styles` set (opacity, colours, border widths/colours, margins, paddings, sizes, insets, z-index, font-size, word-spacing, text-indent, flex-grow/shrink, translate-only transform, visibility); `allow-discrete` flips at 50 % for those. A child does not start a transition on an inherited value its transitioning ancestor moved. getComputedStyle keeps the before-change style of what it reads (so "flush, set value + transition, wait" works). Events in step 4 of the rendering update (App `anim_tick`, headless `update_animations`) by phase change; App in-between restyles capped at max(33 ms, 2 x last build), none after a build > 50 ms; headless only at phase changes; nothing running = no wake-up. `is_animated` covers running transitions (incremental re-cascade); the hover patch and the geometry in-place write refuse transition-declaring elements. Tests: src/tests/qanimhlb_tests.rs (11). Gates: --wpt-th dom/events/webkit-transition-end-event 4/13 -> 13/13, EventListener-invoke-legacy 4/6 -> 6/6, dom/nodes moveBefore continue-css-transition-left/-left-pseudo/-transform-pseudo and css-transition-to-disconnected-document 0/1 -> 1/1; continue-css-transition-transform, css-transition-cross-shadow, css-transition-trigger subtest TIMEOUT -> FAIL (moveBefore is remove+insert here, so the transition is cancelled/restarted). Reftest subset unchanged (340/286, incl. the two transition reftests). --perf-report on replayed ytr/ytw/github (2 rounds, alternating, load 3-22): github identical (forced layouts 128, ~5.3-5.7 s both), YouTube within the run-to-run noise (ytr rendering-step layouts 8 -> 9-17: the headless style step now also runs for pages that declare transitions). Live (nested dwl, inject, grim): a 2 s hover background-color/opacity transition shows in-between frames (pixel (0,0,255) -> (170,79,163) -> (224,119,149) -> (255,153,153)), events run/start/end in order, the reverse on leave runs too; idle CPU after it settles 1 tick / 10 s (also after hovers on replayed en.wikipedia). Left out (proposed follow-up): `allow-discrete` for display/content-visibility, `inherit` on the longhands, transform functions beyond translate, CSSTransition objects / `getAnimations()`, the App's getComputedStyle clock between builds, moveBefore keeping a transition.

## QCE1: customized built-ins created by the parser (agent item)

> QCE1 [S] (P3, from QWPTFLK3 #550) Customized built-ins created by the parser: set attributes before the constructor runs, queue attributeChanged/mutation records in the HTML order, `document.anchors` for customized built-ins.

**What changed:** js_dom.rs `customElements.define` run from a parser script (`curScript` with a write point) treats elements that FOLLOW that script as "not parsed yet": `ceParseDetach` silently strips the attributes of all of them first, then `ceUpgrade(..., parse)` runs each constructor on the bare element, appends the attributes one by one through the hooked `__d_setattr` (mutation records + attributeChangedCallback in attribute order), and puts the element back where it was parsed if the constructor moved it. Elements before the script, and later `define()`s, upgrade as before. connectedCallback is no longer fired twice when the re-insert already connected the element. Deviation: the page is still parsed up front, so all constructors run at define() time, not interleaved with later scripts. WPT: parser-sets-attributes-after-built-in-constructor 2/9 -> 9/9, after-autonomous-constructor 1/3 -> 3/3; wpt-th no regression, custom-elements area stable over 5 reruns. Tests: src/tests/qce1_tests.rs.

## QANIMHLc: geometry reads during running CSS animations and transitions (agent item)

> QANIMHLc [S] (P3, from QANIMHL #562; Sonnet; js_geom GeomCache) Geometry reads during a CSS animation: the forced-layout cache is keyed only on the DOM write generation, so getBoundingClientRect of an animated box keeps its first-frame geometry between DOM writes; key on the animation clock too when animations are live.

**What changed:** `GeomCache` keeps `anim_clock`: the document clock of its layout when the style pass behind it saw an animation that has not ended or a running transition (`anim_eval::layout_animated`, set by both `finish_*` report functions). Such a layout is fresh only at the clock a read sees (`anim_eval::read_clock_ms`: the headless task's page clock when set, else the document clock); a layout with nothing animated keeps the old key alone, so pages without running animations lay out exactly as before. A relayout of an animated page moves the document clock to the read clock first (headless adds no frames just to move it, so the clock was a whole frame or more behind; an ended animation or transition is not live and is stable). Tests in src/tests/qanimhlc_tests.rs (animated left/width/transform, transition width, no extra layouts without animations). wpt-th: dom/nodes/moveBefore/css-transition-trigger.html newly passes.

## QAPI6c: "adopted element style reads vh: build true vs engine false" (agent item)

> QAPI6c [S] (P3, from QAPI6 #573; Opus; incr_style.rs) Check-mode mismatch seen once on YouTube results while the window settled ("adopted element style reads vh: build true vs engine false"); build a repro with a height change during load.

**Cause:** selector matching (`matching_indices_for`) evaluates each candidate rule's media list, and a height media query (`(min-height: ..)`, `orientation`, `aspect-ratio`) notes `VIEWPORT_H_READ`. Matches are memoized per build, so the read lands in whichever resolve matches first. A from-scratch build resolves a `display: none` element ONCE (a shown element twice: the display probe in `collect_real_nodes`, then `build_box_for_element`; the second, memo-hit resolve overwrites the record), so its match ran inside that resolve and the record said "reads vh". The engine takes the match from the build's memo before `style_of`, so its own resolve read nothing. Styles identical, only the flag differed. The generated-content walk (counters / quotes) matches elements before the boxes are built when the page's rules need it, and the height media rules come with later sheets: likely why it showed on one load only (not confirmed live). **Not a staleness bug:** which rules match under a height media query is handled by the engine's full re-match on a height change (`Engine::update`: the height changed and some rule's media reads it), never by the per-element flag, and no cascaded value depends on that read.
**Fix:** `incr_style::match_media` wraps the media test at that one choke point: while a build records, a height read during matching is kept aside (`MATCH_VH`) and folded into the build's global `VIEWPORT_H_READ` at `take_record` (`App::reads_viewport_h` unchanged); outside a recording build it is the plain global note as before. Keyframe selection (`@keyframes` inside a height media, `animation.rs`) still marks the element itself. Tests in `src/tests/qapi6c_tests.rs` (check mode, panic off, empty mismatch report): the hidden element under a height media rule adopts cleanly, then four height changes across the threshold keep engine == build (the rule flips, a `10vh` element follows); a hidden element's own `vh` length keeps its flag (only it re-cascades); the same with adoption unverified (`SCRATCHY_INCR=1`). The first test fails without the fix with exactly the YouTube line.

## QCSS-A: SVG paint properties from stylesheets (agent item)

> QCSS-A [S] (P2, from QAPI8 #578 R66 section 4; Sonnet; css.rs, svg paint) SVG `fill`/`stroke`/`stroke-width`/`stroke-linecap` from stylesheets onto inline SVG (8 sites, 1 427 hits: icons render black today).

**What changed:** css.rs `Declarations::svg` (`fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-linecap`, `stroke-linejoin`, `fill-opacity`, `stroke-opacity`, canonical text via `parse_svg_prop`; the CSS-wide keywords go through `wide_keys`). style.rs `SvgProps` (interned, `ComputedStyle::svg`/`InheritedStyle::svg`, all inherited; `decl` bits = declared by CSS on this element) cascaded by `cascade_svg` (nothing declared: the parent pointer, no cost). images.rs `serialize_inline_svg_styled` writes the cascaded values into `style` attributes of the root (also what it inherited from HTML ancestors, unless it has the presentation attribute) and of every descendant (styled through `resolve_style`, so `var()`, `!important`, inline style and the engine table all apply); `currentColor` resolves against the element's own `color`. CSS beats presentation attributes, which beat inheritance. Incremental engine: `svg` is a Box-class field in `style_diff` and part of `inherited_changed`; a hover rule declaring these properties is `Effect::Layout` (the svg is rasterised at build time). qy53n2/qy53n3 expectations that pinned `fill` as a value-judged hover change were updated. Tests: src/tests/qcss_a_tests.rs.
